definition_zh: 人口众多的；人口稠密的；（把一种生物寄居在另一种生物体内的栖息状态）寄居的
definition_en: having a large number of people living in a place, or used of an organism that lives on or inside another organism
core_image: 一片山坡上挤满亮着灯的窗户，人声与灯光密密麻麻
scene: 傍晚的城市边缘，山坡上一排排小窗接连亮起，屋里坐满了人。The populous northern plain shelters nearly half of the country.
sceneCN: 这里 populous 是「人口众多的」（第 1 个义项：一个地方住着大量居民）；句意为这条人口密集的北部平原容纳了全国近一半的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：人口众多的；人口稠密的；寄居的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根 popul- 加名词后缀构成，义为「人口；全体居民」
由拉丁词根 popul- 加动词后缀构成，义为「居住于；使人口聚居」
与 populous 同源，词根义为「人民」，引申为「受大众喜爱的；流行的」
经法语进入英语，义为「平民；大众；百姓」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「人口稠密」

senses.title: Full of people
senses.definition: having a large number of people living in it
senses.definitionCN: 住着大量居民的，人多的
senses.example: China is one of the most populous countries in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 中国是世界上人口最多的国家之一。
senses.why: The Latin adjective populosus means full of people, from populus, the people, so the first sense is simply the place packed with them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 populosus 意为「满是人的」，来自 populus「人民」，所以第一义项就是把居民装满一个地方。

senses.title: Thickly settled
senses.definition: so heavily settled that people are crowded together within a small area
senses.definitionCN: 居民聚集得过密，以致在小片区域内人挤人的
senses.example: Traffic is heavy in the populous suburbs around the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 港口周围人口稠密的郊区交通拥堵。
senses.why: Once a place is full of people, the second sense measures how tightly they are packed, so populous can describe density as well as size.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方一旦住满人，第二义项就转而衡量人挤得有多密，因此 populous 既指数量也指密度。

senses.title: Living on another organism
senses.definition: used in biology of a species that lives in or on the body of another kind of living thing
senses.definitionCN: 生物学用语，指生活于另一种生物体内或体表的物种
senses.example: Populous insects cluster on the underside of the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 寄居的昆虫聚在叶片背面。
senses.why: The same image of crowding is turned inward: one kind of life crowds onto the body of another, and older biology used the word for such hangers-on.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「挤在一起」的画面被转向内部：一种生物挤在另一种生物身体上，早期生物学就用这个词指这类依附者。

intro.en: Populous goes back to the Latin populus, the people, through the adjective populosus, and it is a direct Latin loan rather than a word that came through French.
intro.cn: populous 经拉丁语形容词 populosus 追溯到 populus「人民」，是直接从拉丁语借入的词，不经过法语。

items.en: Populus means the people or the common people. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and some older explanations linking it to words for abundance are not accepted by modern handbooks.
items.cn: populus 意为「人民、平民」。它更早的来源不确定，一些旧说把它与表示「丰盛」的词联系起来，现代辞书并不接受。

items.en: The adjective populosus meant full of people or thickly peopled, built from populus with the suffix -osus, meaning full of.
items.cn: 形容词 populosus 意为「满是人的、人口稠密的」，由 populus 加后缀 -osus「充满……的」构成。

items.en: Renaissance writers revived classical Latin words directly, and populous entered English learning as a literal Latin loan.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的写作者直接复活古典拉丁语词，populous 作为字面直译借词进入英语书面语。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English in the fifteenth century, applied to countries, cities and regions. The exact first source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词十五世纪首次见于英语记录，用于国家、城市与地区。确切的首见出处不确定。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the geographic sense, while biology once used populous for species that crowd onto a host organism.
items.cn: 现代用法保留地理义，生物学一度用 populous 指挤在宿主身上的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the Latin root populus, the people, or merely resemble populous in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of population, crowding and emptiness.
note.cn: 形近组收与拉丁词根 populus「人民」同源的词，或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收描述人口、拥挤与空寂的形容词。

entries.definition: To fill a place with people or animals; the verb built on the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住于；使人口聚居」，与 populous 同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The people who live in a place, or the total number of them; a close relative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人口；全体居民」，与 populous 同根。

entries.definition: Relating to a political movement that claims to speak for ordinary people; it shares the people root but has its own political meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「民粹主义的、民粹派」，同出「人民」词根，但在政治语境中有专门含义。

entries.definition: A tall fast-growing tree; it only looks close to populous and comes from a quite different source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杨树」，一种高大速生的树；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The noun meaning the state of being crowded with people; formed from populous plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人口稠密」，由 populous 加后缀 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Having too many people or things in one place; spoken of streets, rooms and vehicles rather than whole regions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「拥挤的」，多形容街道、房间、车辆，而不是整片地区。

entries.definition: In a tightly packed way; commonly paired with populated in the fixed phrase densely populated.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「稠密地」，常与 populated 搭配成 densely populated「人口稠密的」。

entries.definition: Inhabited by people; used mostly in compounds such as densely populated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有人居住的」，多见于 densely populated 这类复合表达。

entries.definition: So full that movement is blocked; stresses the resulting jams and problems, not the head count alone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「拥堵的、阻塞的」，强调由此造成的堵塞与麻烦，而不只是人数多。

entries.definition: Empty of people because everyone has left; the opposite of populous in the sense of full homes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「空无一人的、废弃的」，与 populous 的「住满人」正好相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root populus and the fixed phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 populus，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Populus is the people, and populous is the place that is full of them.
normal.cn: populus 是「人民」，populous 就是装满了人的地方。

normal.en: The -ous ending means full of, as in populous: full of people.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ous 表示「充满……的」，所以 populous 就是「充满人的」。

normal.en: Population is the people themselves, populous describes the place they fill.
normal.cn: population 是人口本身，populous 则形容人口填充的那个地方。

normal.en: The news often says most populous country, meaning the one with the largest number of people.
normal.cn: 新闻常说 most populous country，指人口数量最多的国家。

normal.en: Compare popular: popular is liked by people, populous is filled with people.
normal.cn: 对比 popular：popular 是被人喜欢的，populous 是被人住满的。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside where every window is lit and every step leads to another lit room.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山坡，每扇窗都亮着灯，每走一步又进到另一间亮灯的屋子。

abstract.en: Think of a map where one district is covered in tiny dots until the colour of the paper disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，其中一区被小圆点铺满，直到纸的底色都看不见了。

abstract.en: Picture a swarm of tiny insects on a single leaf, one kind of life crowded onto another.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子上密布小虫，一种生命挤在另一种生命之上。

examples.en: The report compares the coastline of the least populated islands with the most populous metropolises.
examples.cn: 报告把人口最少的海岛海岸线与人口最多的都市进行了对比。

examples.en: Because the city is so populous, the metro runs every two minutes at peak hours.
examples.cn: 由于这座城市人口众多，地铁在高峰时段每两分钟就发一趟。

examples.en: The northern plains are far more populous than the dry plateau to the west.
examples.cn: 北部平原的人口远比西边的干燥高原要密集。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡皮勒斯」——人群像泡皮一样密密冒出来，就是「人口众多」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 populus「人民、平民」+ 后缀 -osus「充满……的」→ populosus「满是人的」→ 英语 populous「人口众多的」。同根的英语族词包括 population、populate、popular、populace；populus 更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Populous starts from the place that is full of people, then measures how tightly they are packed, and finally applies the same crowding image to a species living on a host organism.
sensesIntro.cn: populous 先指住满人的地方，再衡量人挤得有多密，最后把同样的「挤在一起」画面用于寄居在宿主身上的物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside of windows all lit at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片山坡上所有窗户同时亮起。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a country, city or province whose total number of residents is large.
branches.cn: 地点线：全国、城市或省份的居民总数很多。

branches.en: THE DENSITY: the same people packed into a small area, so walks, homes and roads are crowded.
branches.cn: 密度线：同样的人挤在小片区域，于是街道、住宅与道路都很拥挤。

branches.en: THE HOST: biology applies the crowding image inside a body, where one species lives on another.
branches.cn: 宿主线：生物学把「拥挤」意象挪到生物体内，一种生物依附另一种生活。

branches.en: Both branches share the Latin image of a population that fills a space to its edge.
branches.cn: 两条分支都共享拉丁语中人口把空间填到边缘的画面。

branches.en: Houses full of families and hosts full of parasites are two ways of saying somebody is crowded onto somebody else.
branches.cn: 住满家庭的房屋与住满寄生物的宿主，都是把甲者挤在乙者之上。

intro.en: Populous is a Latin adjective built from a noun and the suffix -osus; English then borrows and extends it with -ness.
intro.cn: populous 是拉丁语中以名词加后缀 -osus 构成的形容词，英语借入后再用 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin populus, populosus and populari are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European origin of populus is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 populus、populosus、populari 均有文献记录，只有 populus 更早的印欧来源属于不确定的推测。

items.example: The root comes from Latin populus.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根来自拉丁语 populus。

items.example: Populus is the direct source of the word family.
items.exampleCN: populus 是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -osus forms populosus.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -osus 构成 populosus。

items.example: Populosus is the direct Latin model for populous.
items.exampleCN: populosus 是 populous 的直接拉丁语原型。

items.example: The ending -ous carries the full of meaning into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把「充满」的含义带入英语。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms populate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 populate。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms population.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 population。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms populousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 populousness。

items.meaning: the state of being crowded with people
items.example: Populousness describes a crowded land.
items.exampleCN: populousness 描述人满为患的土地。

definition_en: a hard, white, shiny material made by firing fine clay at high heat, or objects made of it
core_image: 一只薄得透光的白瓷杯，敲一下发出清亮的响声
scene: 老茶馆的木柜里摆着一整套白瓷茶具，杯壁薄得能透出灯光。She lifted the delicate porcelain cup and heard a clear note when she tapped it.
sceneCN: 这里 porcelain 是「瓷器」（第 1 个义项：用高温烧制的硬质白色器皿）；句意为她举起那只精巧的瓷杯，轻敲时听到一声清亮的回响。

pos.zh: 名词：瓷；瓷器；瓷质材料
形容词：瓷制的；瓷一般的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加拉丁式形容词后缀构成，义为「瓷质的；像瓷的」
porcelaneous 的常见异体拼写，义为「瓷质的」
由本词词根加矿物后缀 -ite 构成，义为「瓷状岩、瓷石」，一种致密的沉积岩

senses.title: Hard white ceramic ware
senses.definition: a hard, smooth, white or translucent material produced by firing pure white clay at very high temperature
senses.definitionCN: 用纯净白瓷土经极高温烧制而成的坚硬、光滑、白色或半透明的材料
senses.example: The museum keeps a collection of porcelain from the Ming period.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆收藏了一批明代瓷器。
senses.why: The Italian name comes from porcella, a small sow, because the glossy shell of a cowrie was thought to look like a piglet, so porcelain first pictured something hard and shell-like.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语名来自 porcella「小母猪」，因为光亮的贝壳被认为像小猪，所以 porcelain 最初画的就是坚硬如壳的材料。

senses.title: Objects made of it
senses.definition: cups, plates, figurines and other objects made from this fired clay material
senses.definitionCN: 用这种烧制黏土制成的杯子、盘子、人偶等器物
senses.example: She washed the porcelain by hand to keep the gilt from fading.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手洗这些瓷器，以免描金褪色。
senses.why: Once the material became a marked good, it came to name the goods themselves, so the mass noun turns countable when we speak of individual pieces.
senses.whyCN: 材料一旦成为商品，就转而指商品本身，于是这个不可数名词在指一件件器物时可以变作可数。

senses.title: Like porcelain
senses.definition: used as an adjective to describe something made of this material or as smooth and delicate as it
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，表示由此材料制成，或像瓷一样光滑细腻
senses.example: The dancer had pale porcelain skin.
senses.exampleCN: 那位舞者皮肤白皙，宛如瓷器。
senses.why: The hard white shell image spreads from material to appearance, and porcelain becomes a ready-made comparison for smoothness and pallor.
senses.whyCN: 坚白的外壳意象从材料扩散到外观，porcelain 就成了形容光滑与苍白的现成比喻。

intro.en: Porcelain is a wanderer: an Italian name built on a piglet, carried through French, yet naming a craft that reached Europe from China.
intro.cn: porcelain 是个漂泊者：意大利语名来自「小猪」，经法语进入英语，命名的却是一门从中国传到欧洲的工艺。

items.en: Travelers in the eastern Mediterranean used porcellana for the polished cowrie shell, and the name spread along the trade routes to Chinese ceramic ware.
items.cn: 东地中海的旅行者用 porcellana 称光亮的海贝，这个名字沿贸易路线传开，也用来称中国的陶瓷器。

items.en: Porcellana probably comes from porcella, a small sow, in reference to the shape of the cowrie; this cankered-shell explanation is traditional rather than certain, and other accounts have been proposed.
items.cn: porcellana 一般认为来自 porcella「小母猪」，取其形似贝壳之意；这一解释是传统的、并非定论，学界也提出过其他说法。

items.en: French porcelaine fixed the spelling with the -aine ending, and the word reached European writing through the craze for imported Chinese ware.
items.cn: 法语 porcelaine 以 -aine 词尾固定拼写，并借进口中国瓷器的热潮进入欧洲书面语。

items.en: English borrows it as porcelaine in the late sixteenth century and later settles on porcelain. The exact first attestation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪后期以 porcelaine 借入，后来固定为 porcelain。确切的最早出处不确定。

items.en: European workshops learned to fire true hard-paste porcelain in the eighteenth century, and the word broadened from imported ware to any piece of fine ceramic.
items.cn: 欧洲工坊在十八世纪学会烧制真正的硬质瓷，这个词也从进口器物扩展到一切精细陶瓷制品。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the Italian piglet or cowrie story, or merely resemble porcelain in shape; the near-meaning group gathers pottery terms of different fineness.
note.cn: 形近组收分享同一「小猪与贝壳」典故或只是形似的词；近义组收不同精细程度的陶器术语。

entries.definition: The Italian word for cowrie shell and later for Chinese ceramic ware; the direct source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语，先指海贝，后指中国陶瓷器，是英语 porcelain 的直接来源。

entries.definition: Italian for a small sow; said to be the source of the shell name on which porcelain rests.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语，意为「小母猪」；一般认为正是它构成了贝壳名，再衍生出 porcelain。

entries.definition: Relating to pigs; it shares the Latin pig root porcus but is not the source of porcelain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「猪的、像猪的」；它确实同出拉丁语「猪」的来源，但与 porcelain 并非同一派生链。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning like porcelain; formed from porcelain with a Latin-style ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「瓷质的；像瓷的」，由 porcelain 加拉丁式形容词词尾构成。

entries.definition: The state of having tiny holes; it starts with the same letters but comes from Greek poros, a passage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多孔性、孔隙度」；字母开头相似，但来自希腊语 poros「通道」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The everyday word for porcelain goods in British English, named after the country that made them.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语里指瓷器的日常用词，得名于产地中国。

entries.definition: The broad term for fired clay objects of every grade, from bricks to fine ware.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指一切烧制黏土器物的宽泛术语，从砖瓦到精细器皿都算。

entries.definition: Earthen vessels and the craft of making them; plainer and softer than porcelain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陶器、陶艺」，比 porcelain 更朴素、质地也更软。

entries.definition: Porous pottery fired at a lower temperature, opaque and often glazed; the opposite of porcelain in fineness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陶器」，低温烧成、多孔不透明，精细程度与瓷器相反。

entries.definition: Pottery fired high enough to be dense and non-porous, but not as white or translucent as porcelain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「炻器、石器」，烧成致密不渗水，但不如瓷器洁白透亮。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Italian piglet story and the ordinary phrases porcelain actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子使用真实的意大利语「小猪」典故，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The Italian name rests on porcella, a small sow, because the glossy cowrie shell looked like a piglet.
normal.cn: 意大利语名建于 porcella「小母猪」之上，因为光亮的贝壳看起来像小猪。

normal.en: Porcelain is fired at very high heat from pure white clay, so it is harder and whiter than pottery.
normal.cn: 瓷器由纯净白瓷土经极高温烧成，所以比陶器更坚硬、更洁白。

normal.en: In British English, china is the everyday word for the same goods.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，china 就是同类器物的日常说法。

normal.en: A porcelain figurine is small and fragile, so museums display them behind glass.
normal.cn: porcelain figurine 是又小又易碎的瓷人偶，博物馆都把这类展品放在玻璃柜里。

normal.en: Compare ceramic: ceramic is the whole family, porcelain is the whitest and finest member.
normal.cn: 对比 ceramic：ceramic 是整族的上位词，porcelain 是其中最白、最精细的一支。

abstract.en: Hold a cup so thin that a lamp behind it glows through the wall.
abstract.cn: 手里握一只薄杯，背后的灯光能透过杯壁照出来。

abstract.en: Tap the rim with a fingernail and listen for the clear, ringing note.
abstract.cn: 用指甲轻敲杯沿，听那清亮的回声。

abstract.en: See a pale arm that looks like polished shell, cool and smooth to the touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条苍白的手臂，像打磨过的贝壳，触手冰凉光滑。

examples.en: The tea house serves its oolong in thin porcelain cups.
examples.cn: 这家茶馆用薄瓷杯盛乌龙茶。

examples.en: Exported porcelain from Jingdezhen once filled the cabinets of wealthy European families.
examples.cn: 景德镇外销的瓷器曾摆满欧洲富裕家庭的橱柜。

examples.en: There is a collection of painted porcelain in the east hall.
examples.cn: 东厅里陈列着一批彩绘瓷器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖色脸」——把一只瓷碗剖开，断面白得像玉一样；这只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 意大利语 porcellana（海贝，转指中国瓷器）一般认为源于 porcella「小母猪」，取其形似贝壳之意；经法语 porcelaine 于十六世纪进入英语，最终写作 porcelain。中文语境常称「瓷器」，与英文词根无直接关系。

sensesIntro.en: Porcelain first names the fired white material, then the objects made from it, and finally serves as a comparison for anything smooth and pale.
sensesIntro.cn: porcelain 先指烧成的白色瓷质材料，再指用这种材料制成的器物，最后用作形容光滑苍白的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shell so smooth and bright that it becomes a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：光滑发亮的外壳最后变成了一只手可持的杯子。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: hard, white, translucent clay fired at extreme heat.
branches.cn: 材料线：经极高温烧成、坚硬洁白且半透明的瓷土。

branches.en: THE GOODS: the countable pieces, from cups and plates to figurines and vases.
branches.cn: 器物线：一件件实物，从杯盘到人偶与花瓶。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: the same shell-like gloss used to describe skin, teeth or a vase-like finish.
branches.cn: 比喻线：同一种贝壳般的光泽被用来形容皮肤、牙齿或釉面。

branches.en: Both readings rest on the foreign craft that Europe first knew only as imported treasure.
branches.cn: 两种读法都建立在欧洲最初只当作进口珍宝的异邦工艺之上。

branches.en: The shell that gave the name also gave the image of a surface both hard and glowing.
branches.cn: 赋予其名的贝壳，也赋予了「坚硬而发亮」的表面意象。

intro.en: Porcelain is not built from English pieces; its parts are the Italian porcella and the endings that settled the spelling in France and England.
intro.cn: porcelain 并非由英语构件组成，它的构件是意大利语的 porcella，以及最终在法国和英格兰固定下来的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The deeper Latin base is porcus, a pig, seen in porcine and in the French porc; the Italian dimorphic forms are the keys to the family.
latinIntro.cn: 更深一层的拉丁底子是 porcus「猪」，拉丁语的 porcine 与法语 porc 都保留了它；理解这一族词，要靠意大利语的诸形。

items.example: The root porc- enters Italian through Latin porcus.
items.exampleCN: 词根 porc- 经拉丁语 porcus 进入意大利语。

items.example: Porcella is the traditional basis of the name.
items.exampleCN: porcella 是这个名字流传已久的根据。

items.example: Porcellana moved from shell to tableware.
items.exampleCN: porcellana 由贝壳转指餐具。

items.meaningCN: 构成材料类名词的词尾
items.example: The ending -ana shapes porcellana.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ana 构成 porcellana。

items.example: French fixed the spelling with -aine.
items.exampleCN: 法语用 -aine 固定了拼写。

items.meaning: forming a noun, often a material
items.example: The ending -ine ends porcelain.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ine 收束了 porcelain。

items.example: The suffix -eous forms porcelaneous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eous 构成 porcelaneous。

items.example: Porcelaneous describes a shell-like surface.
items.exampleCN: porcelaneous 形容类似瓷面的表面。

items.example: The suffix -ite forms porcelanite.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ite 构成 porcelanite。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加拉丁式形容词后缀构成，义为「瓷质的；像瓷的」
porcelaneous 的常见异体拼写，义为「瓷质的」
由本词词根加矿物后缀 -ite 构成，义为「瓷状岩、瓷石」，一种致密的沉积岩

definition_zh: 门廊；外廊；（美式房屋正门前的）前廊
definition_en: a covered shelter or veranda built onto the outside of a building, especially at an entrance; in American English, a raised covered platform in front of a house
core_image: 屋檐伸出一截，门前由廊柱撑起的一小块带顶空地
scene: 夏夜，屋檐下的长凳上坐着乘凉的邻居，双脚刚跨过那道矮台阶。We sat on the porch until the stars came out.
sceneCN: 这里 porch 是「门廊」（第 1 个义项：从屋檐下伸出、带顶的入口空间）；句意为我们一直坐在门廊里，直到星星出来。

pos.zh: 名词：门廊；外廊；前廊；（教堂等的）门廊
动词（古语、方言）：在门廊上停留；使通向门廊

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「带有门廊的」，如 a porched house「有门廊的房子」
近亲词（不同拼写），拉丁语 porta「门」的同源词，义为「门廊、柱廊」，形容整体由柱列支撑的入口建筑
近亲词（法语借入），法语 porte「门」+ cochere，义为「车道门廊、车廊」，供马车或汽车进出时遮风挡雨

senses.title: A covered entrance to a building
senses.definition: a covered shelter built out from the wall of a building, forming the entrance and sheltering the door
senses.definitionCN: 从建筑外墙向外伸出、带顶的遮蔽结构，构成入口并为大门遮风挡雨
senses.example: She waited in the porch while her boots dried.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门廊里等靴子晾干。
senses.why: The word descends from Latin porta, a door, with the Latin porticus giving a colonnaded passage, so the first sense is the sheltered space wrapped around the door.
senses.whyCN: 这个词溯源于拉丁语 porta「门」，并经拉丁语 porticus 获得「柱廊通道」的意思，所以第一义项就是那处环绕着门、带顶的空间。

senses.title: A veranda open to the air
senses.definition: a long covered platform along the side of a house, open at the front and used for sitting outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 沿房屋一侧延伸的长而带顶的平台，正面敞开，供人们在室外坐着乘凉
senses.example: The neighbours chatted on the screened porch until late.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们在纱窗门廊上聊天到很晚。
senses.why: On colonial houses in warm climates the entrance grew into a long open veranda, so the same word came to mean the place people use in the evening heat.
senses.whyCN: 在炎热气候的殖民风格住宅上，入口渐渐长成了长而敞开的外廊，于是同一个词也指人们在暑夜消磨时光的那个地方。

senses.title: The classic front stoop
senses.definition: in North American usage, a raised covered platform with steps in front of a house, used as an informal outdoor room
senses.definitionCN: 北美用法中，房屋正门前带台阶的带顶平台，被当作室外的非正式起居空间
senses.example: Everyone on the street seemed to be out on the porch that evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那天傍晚街坊们似乎都到前廊上待着。
senses.why: The short covered entrance steps into American domestic life turned it into a social room, so the word now names a specific feature of ordinary American housing.
senses.whyCN: 带顶的短入口台阶成了美国日常生活的舞台，于是它被当作一个社交性的房间，这个词如今也指普通美式住宅的特定部件。

intro.en: Porch reaches back through Old French and Latin to a root meaning a passage or a doorway, and its sense of a covered entrance grew out of a colonnaded walk.
intro.cn: porch 经古法语与拉丁语追溯到意为「通道、门口」的词根，其「带顶入口」之义正是从柱廊通道的含义中长出来的。

items.en: Porticus meant a covered walk or colonnade before a building, built on Latin porta, a door or gate.
items.cn: porticus 意为建筑物前带顶的步道或柱廊，由拉丁语 porta「门、门道」构成。

items.en: Old French porche narrowed the colonnade to the covered entrance or gallery in front of a church.
items.cn: 古法语 porche 把宽泛的柱廊收窄为教堂前带顶的入口或廊厅。

items.en: The family differs by one letter, portus versus porta: portus gives port and meant a harbour, understood as an opening, while porta gives portal and porch and meant a door.
items.cn: 这一族只差一个字母，portus 对 porta：portus 生出 port「港口」，本义是「开口」，而 porta 生出 portal 与 porch，本义是「门」。

items.en: Porch enters Middle English around the thirteenth century, first applied to vestibules and covered entrances of buildings. The exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: porch 约在十三世纪进入中古英语，最初指建筑的门厅与带顶入口。确切的首次记录不确定。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the word widened from churches and halls to ordinary houses, giving the front porch its own name.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词从教堂与厅堂扩展到普通民居，住宅前廊因此有了专门的名称。

items.en: The American front porch became a social room of the neighbourhood, and the word kept that resonance to the present.
items.cn: 美国式前廊成为邻里之间的社交空间，这一意涵一直保留到今天。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin door and passage stems; the near-meaning group gathers the covered outdoor spaces porch is often confused with.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一拉丁语「门、通道」词干构成的词；近义组收常与 porch 混淆的带顶室外空间词。

entries.definition: A structure with columns supporting a roof above a walkway, often at a temple or public building entrance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「柱廊、门廊」，指以柱列支撑屋盖、下有步道的结构，常见于神庙或公共建筑入口。

entries.definition: A grand doorway or gate, or the entrance to a website; built on the Latin porta.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大门、正门」或「门户网站」，直接出自拉丁语 porta「门」。

entries.definition: A heavy sliding grating in a castle gate; the first part is the same Latin porta.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「城堡闸门、铁闸」，前半部分同样出自拉丁语 porta「门」。

entries.definition: A harbour where ships load; it comes from portus, meaning an opening, not from the porta of porch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「港口」，出自 portus「开口」，而不是 porch 所用 porta「门」，两者只是形近且上游相关。

entries.definition: A small soft bag; it merely looks close to porch and comes from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小袋、荷包、育儿袋」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A long roofed gallery attached to the outside of a house, warmer and usually on one side; often confused with porch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「游廊、外廊」，附在房屋外侧的长廊，多见于炎热地区，常与 porch 混用。

entries.definition: In New York and New England usage, the steps and small landing before a house entrance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门前台阶」，纽约与新英格兰一带专指房屋入口前的台阶和小平台。

entries.definition: A flat paved area beside a house, sometimes raised and roofed; wider and often walled.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「平台、露台」，房屋旁平整铺砌的地面，常带矮墙，范围更宽敞。

entries.definition: A small platform above ground level, reached from an upstairs window or door.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「阳台」，位于地面之上、从楼上窗门出入的小平台。

entries.definition: An enclosed entrance hall inside a building; the porch is the same entrance turned outward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门厅、前室」，位于建筑内部，而 porch 是同一种入口向外翻转的部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin door phrase and the phrases porch actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「门」的来源，以及 porch 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Porch and portal share the Latin porta, a door: the porch is the roof added over the door.
normal.cn: porch 与 portal 同出拉丁语 porta「门」：porch 就是加在门上面的那层屋檐。

normal.en: Porticus meant a colonnade, and porche in Old French meant the covered entrance of a church.
normal.cn: porticus 指柱廊，古法语的 porche 指教堂带顶的入口。

normal.en: The plural is porches: add -es after the ch sound, as in churches.
normal.cn: 复数是 porches：ch 音结尾要加 -es，正如 churches。

normal.en: On the porch is the usual phrase, meaning the porch and its bench are the place to sit.
normal.cn: 常用搭配是 on the porch，意思是 porch 以及它上面的长凳就是坐着的地方。

normal.en: Compare port and porta: port is a harbour from portus, porch is a door from porta.
normal.cn: 对比 port 与 porta：port 出自 portus 的港口，porch 出自 porta 的门。

abstract.en: Picture a column, two columns, and then a whole row, holding up a roof that keeps the rain off the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柱子、两根柱子，然后一整排，撑起一片让雨落不到门上的屋顶。

abstract.en: See a short flight of steps from the street up to a bench where neighbours face each other.
abstract.cn: 想象从街上几级矮台阶上来，就是一张让邻居们面对面坐着的长凳。

abstract.en: Feel the skin between the open air and the kitchen: the porch is the one place both sides can see.
abstract.cn: 感受室外与厨房之间的那层皮：porch 是能同时望见两边的地方。

examples.en: The rain drummed on the porch roof all afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午，雨点敲打着门廊的屋顶。

examples.en: They painted the porches of every house on the street white.
examples.cn: 他们把街上每户人家的门廊都刷成了白色。

examples.en: Excuse me, could you wait under the porch while I find an umbrella?
examples.cn: 劳驾，您能先在门廊下等一会儿吗，我去找把伞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡赤」——门前是坡地，也被屋檐护住一块红色的砖台，那就是门廊；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 porta「门、门道」+ 通道义的 porticus「柱廊」→ 古法语 porche「教堂前带顶的入口」→ 中古英语 porch「门厅、入口」→ 现代英语 porch「门廊、前廊」。同族的 portal 直接出自 porta，而 port「港口」出自形近的 portus「开口」。

sensesIntro.en: Porch begins as the shelter built over a door, widens into the open veranda of warm climates, and settles as the raised front platform of American homes.
sensesIntro.cn: porch 起初是罩在门上的遮蔽结构，继而扩展为炎热气候下的敞开外廊，最终固定为美式住宅门前那座带台阶的平台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roof lifted out from the wall so the door has a dry place.
core.cn: 核心意象：从墙上伸出的一片屋檐，让门前有了干燥的一小块地方。

branches.en: THE GATE: the porch protects the door, and the earliest uses name the entry to a church or hall.
branches.cn: 大门线：porch 保护着那扇门，最早的用法正指教堂或厅堂的入口。

branches.en: THE VERANDA: the entrance stretches along the wall and opens to the air, becoming a place to sit.
branches.cn: 外廊线：入口沿墙拉长并向空中敞开，成为一个可以久坐的地方。

branches.en: THE STOP: the front platform with steps turns a doorway into a semi-public room of the street.
branches.cn: 平台线：带台阶的前廊把一扇门变成了半公开的街坊空间。

branches.en: Both are covered and both belong to the wall, but one faces the door and one faces the evening.
branches.cn: 两者都带顶、都依附于墙面，只是一个朝向门，一个朝向傍晚。

branches.en: Both branches turn the entrance into a room outdoors, so porches and verandas often overlap in speech.
branches.cn: 两条分支都把入口变成室外房间，所以口语里 porch 与 veranda 常互相指代。

intro.en: Porch itself has no English affix; it is a whole Latin word shrunk by French. Its family grows through related Latin stems for door and passage.
intro.cn: porch 自身没有英语词缀，它是被法语缩简过的完整拉丁词；它的词族靠拉丁语「门、通道」相关词干发展。

latinIntro.en: Latin porta, porticus and portus are all recorded, differing by one letter and one meaning: a door, a colonnade, a harbour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 porta、porticus、portus 均有文献记录，只差一个字母与一层含义：门、柱廊、港口。

items.example: Porta is the direct Latin base of the word.
items.exampleCN: porta 是这个单词的直接拉丁语基础。

items.example: Porticus adds the colonnade image.
items.exampleCN: porticus 增加了柱廊的意象。

items.example: Portus gives the look-alike port.
items.exampleCN: portus 生出形近的 port。

items.example: Porche carries the word into English.
items.exampleCN: porche 把这个词带入英语。

items.meaning: a French spelling kept in English
items.meaningCN: 保留在英语中的法语拼写现象
items.example: The ending -ch is the French spelling kept in English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ch 是英语保留的法语拼写。

items.meaning: plural after ch, sh, s sounds
items.example: The ending -es forms porches.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 porches。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms porched.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 porched。

items.example: Portal is built directly on Latin porta.
items.exampleCN: portal 直接建于拉丁语 porta 之上。

items.example: Portico comes from the same porticus line.
items.exampleCN: portico 与 porticus 同出一线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「带有门廊的」，如 a porched house「有门廊的房子」
近亲词（不同拼写），同出拉丁语 porta「门」的一线，义为「柱廊、门廊」，指整体由柱列支撑的入口建筑
近亲词（不同拼写），直接出自拉丁语 porta「门」，义为「大门、正门；门户网站」

definition_zh: 鼠海豚；海豚科动物；鼠海豚属成员
definition_en: a small sea mammal with a rounded head and a short beak, closely related to dolphins but usually quieter and more compact
core_image: 海面上露出一个圆钝的小脑袋，背脊一拱就沉下去
scene: 清晨的港湾很安静，远处水面忽然浮起一个小黑影，拱了一下背又潜了下去。A porpoise surfaced briefly beside the fishing boat and vanished.
sceneCN: 这里 porpoise 是「鼠海豚」（第 1 个义项：一种体型小、头圆的海兽）；句意是：一只鼠海豚在渔船旁短暂浮出水面，随即消失不见。场景中可见的物件有渔船的船舷和起伏的水面。

pos.zh: 名词：鼠海豚；海豚类小型鲸类
动词（罕见）：露头透气；浮出水面

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -like 构成，义为「像鼠海豚的」
由动词加 -ing 名词化，指「有轨电车杆反复脱轨、火车票反复补退（非正式）」；在动物学中也可作名词指鼠海豚露头行为
由属名词形 Phocoena 加后缀构成，指「鼠海豚科动物」（动物学术语）

senses.title: A small sea mammal with a blunt snout
senses.titleCN: 鼠海豚：头圆喙短的小型海兽
senses.definition: a small, stocky marine mammal related to dolphins, with a rounded head and a short, blunt beak
senses.definitionCN: 一种体型粗短、与海豚同科的小型海洋哺乳动物，头圆、喙短而钝
senses.example: A harbour porpoise swam past the pier at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，一只港湾鼠海豚游过了码头。
senses.why: The name comes from pig plus fish, so the creature was seen as a little sea pig with a blunt face.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「猪」和「鱼」两部分组成，在旧时人的眼里，它就像一头圆嘴的小海猪，于是核心意象可以理解成一头在水里拱来拱去的猪。

senses.title: Any member of the porpoise family
senses.definition: any of the small whale species of the family that includes the harbour porpoise and the finless porpoise
senses.definitionCN: 鼠海豚科的任一小型鲸类物种，包括港湾鼠海豚与江豚等
senses.example: The Yangtze finless porpoise is now one of the rarest porpoises.
senses.exampleCN: 长江江豚如今是最稀有的鼠海豚之一。
senses.why: Once the harbour species gave the name, zoologists used it for a whole family of similar blunt-nosed whales.
senses.whyCN: 港湾鼠海豚先被这么称呼，动物学家随后把名字扩展到整个家族，凡圆头短喙的小型鲸类都归入这一类。

senses.title: A figure of speech for a dolphin
senses.definition: a loose or literary word for a dolphin, used when the writer does not mean a stricter biological distinction
senses.definitionCN: 在诗文或口语中宽松地泛指海豚，并不做严格的生物学区分
senses.example: The sailors called every leaping fish in the bow wave a porpoise.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们把船头浪里每一条跃起的「鱼」都叫作鼠海豚。
senses.why: Ordinary speakers rarely separate the two animals, so the older word spreads over dolphin as an everyday label.
senses.whyCN: 普通人很少分辨海豚与鼠海豚，于是这个更老的日常称呼顺势铺开，泛指那些在船边跳跃的海兽，二者边界就模糊了。

senses.title: The action of surfacing briefly
senses.definition: to come to the surface briefly and dive again, as porpoises do
senses.definitionCN: 像鼠海豚那样短暂浮出水面又潜入水中
senses.example: We watched the seals porpoise in and out of the grey swell.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看着海豹在灰色的浪里露出头又潜下去。
senses.why: Because porpoises surface in quick rolling arcs, their name became a rare verb for that exact motion.
senses.whyCN: 鼠海豚浮出水面的动作短促、成拱形，于是名词本身转化出一个罕见的动词，专门描述这类「冒着拱」的动作。

intro.en: Porpoise joins the Old French words for pig and fish, a calque of Latin porcus marinus, or sea hog.
intro.cn: porpoise 由古法语中表示「猪」和「鱼」的词拼合而来，是对拉丁语 porcus marinus（海猪）的仿译。

items.en: Porcus marinus means sea hog, a blunt-faced sea creature.
items.cn: porcus marinus 意为海猪，指一种圆脸的海中动物。

items.en: Porpeis joins porc, pig, with peis, fish, following the Latin calque.
items.cn: porpeis 把 porc（猪）与 peis（鱼）拼在一起，沿用了拉丁语仿译的思路。

items.en: Forms such as porpays and porpas appear in English records.
items.cn: 中古英语文献中出现了 porpays、porpas 等写法，首见年代大致在这一带，具体年代存疑。

items.en: The spelling settles toward porpoise, with a silent second element.
items.cn: 到了十五至十六世纪，拼写逐渐定型为 porpoise，词尾发音脱落、变得不发音。

items.en: Zoologists give porpoise a precise family meaning, separate from dolphin.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪的动物学把 porpoise 定为科级术语，与 dolphin 明确区分。

items.en: The word spreads to conservation, as the finless porpoise becomes a symbol of river protection.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词进入保护议题，江豚成为河流保护的代表物种。

note.en: Porpoise sits beside its common look-alike dolphin and beside other members of the same sea mammal field.
note.cn: porpoise 最常被拿来和样子相近的 dolphin 比较，也常和同一类海兽场域的名词一起出现。

entries.definition: a hard igneous rock with large crystals set in a fine groundmass
entries.definitionCN: 斑岩，一种晶体嵌在细密基质中的坚硬火成岩；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与porpoise无关

entries.definition: a large rodent covered with spines
entries.definitionCN: 豪猪；与porpoise共用「猪」这个词根，只是第二半成分不同

entries.definition: a small toothed whale with a long beak
entries.definitionCN: 海豚：一种喙较长的齿鲸，与鼠海豚外形相近但并非同一科

entries.definition: any creature that lives in the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海洋动物，泛指活在海里的动物

entries.definition: a mammal that lives mainly in the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海洋哺乳动物，主要生活在海里的哺乳类

entries.definition: the group of small blunt-snouted whales that share this name
entries.definitionCN: 鼠海豚科，共享这一称呼的一组圆头小型鲸类

normalIntro.en: Porpoise is a little sea pig: pig plus fish, dressed in a smooth grey coat.
normalIntro.cn: porpoise 就是一头小海猪：猪加鱼，套着一层光滑的灰外衣。

normal.en: Porpoise hides porc, the old word for pig, and peis, the old word for fish.
normal.cn: porpoise 里藏着表示猪的旧词 porc 和表示鱼的旧词 peis。

normal.en: A harbour porpoise is the species most often seen close to British coasts.
normal.cn: 港湾鼠海豚是英国海岸附近最常见的物种。

normal.en: The finless porpoise, or jiangtun, has no dorsal fin at all.
normal.cn: 江豚（无鳍鼠海豚）背上完全没有背鳍。

normal.en: Unlike dolphins, porpoises have blunt, short beaks and flatter foreheads.
normal.cn: 与海豚不同，鼠海豚的喙短而钝，额头更平。

normal.en: Remember the silent ending: porpoise rhymes with tortoise in its shape, not in sound.
normal.cn: 记住结尾不发音这一点：porpoise 的拼写形状让人想到 tortoise，但读音并无押韵关系。

abstract.en: Picture a grey barrel with a snub nose rolling through a fishing harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个灰色的小桶，顶着平平的鼻子，在渔港的水里翻滚。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole family of blunt-nosed swimmers lined up along a river bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一群圆嘴的游泳健将，沿着河岸排成一列。

abstract.en: Think of an old sailor who calls every leaping back a porpoise.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老水手，看到任何跃起的脊背都喊作鼠海豚。

examples.en: Scientists counted more than three hundred porpoises in the estuary.
examples.cn: 科学家在河口数到了三百多只鼠海豚。

examples.en: The finless porpoise survives in only a few stretches of the great river.
examples.cn: 江豚只在这条大河的几个河段中幸存。

examples.en: Fishing nets remain the biggest threat to the harbour porpoise.
examples.cn: 渔网仍是港湾鼠海豚面临的最大威胁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「跑普斯」——它总在浪里跑来跑去，脑袋一拱就沉下去；这只是读音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 古法语 porc（猪）+ peis（鱼）→ porpeis → 英语 porpoise，仿译拉丁语 porcus marinus（海猪），核心义「圆脸的猪形海兽」。

sensesIntro.en: Porpoise starts as a concrete animal name, spreads to the whole family, loosens into a poetic dolphin word, and finally becomes a verb for its rolling dive.
sensesIntro.cn: porpoise 先是一个具体的动物名，接着扩展到整个科，再在诗文里宽松地泛指海豚，最后转化为动词，指那种翻滚式的露头潜游。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small grey head that rolls up out of the water and down again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个灰色的小脑袋从水面拱出，又沉下去。

branches.en: The single small mammal with a blunt face is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一只圆脸的小型哺乳动物是最日常的义项。

branches.en: The family name collects all similar small whales.
branches.cn: 科名把相似的小型鲸类都收了进来。

branches.en: Everyday speech blurs the line with dolphin.
branches.cn: 日常说法把鼠海豚与海豚的界线模糊了。

branches.en: The rolling dive is the animal turned into a verb.
branches.cn: 翻滚式的潜游就是这只动物被用成了动词。

branches.en: A strict zoological sense and a loose literary sense live side by side.
branches.cn: 严格的动物学义项与宽松的文学义项并存。

intro.en: Porpoise is a compound, pig plus fish, with no English affix of its own.
intro.cn: porpoise 是一个复合词，由「猪」与「鱼」两部分拼成，自身不带英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin porcus means pig, and porcus marinus is the sea hog behind the French shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 porcus 意为猪，porcus marinus（海猪）是法语写法背后的原型。

items.example: Porc is the first half of the old French compound.
items.exampleCN: porc 是古法语复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Peis is the fish half of porpeis.
items.exampleCN: peis 是 porpeis 中表示鱼的那一半。

items.example: Porpeis reached English as porpays.
items.exampleCN: porpeis 以 porpays 的形式进入英语。

items.example: Porpoise is the settled modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: porpoise 是定型的现代拼写。

items.example: The suffix -like forms porpoise-like.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 porpoise-like。

items.example: The suffix -id appears in phocoenid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 出现在 phocoenid 中。

items.example: Porcupine shares the pig root with porpoise.
items.exampleCN: porcupine 与 porpoise 共享「猪」词根。

items.example: Dolphin is the closest everyday contrast word.
items.exampleCN: dolphin 是日常对比中最接近的词。

definition_zh: 姿势；姿态；体态；（比喻）立场、态度；故作姿态
definition_en: the way a person stands, sits, or holds the body, and by extension the attitude a person or group takes toward something
core_image: 一个人站直，脊椎像一摞被摆整齐的积木
scene: 钢琴老师轻轻按住学生的肩膀，让他把背挺直再开始弹。Sit with a straight back and a relaxed posture.
sceneCN: 这里 posture 是「姿势、体态」（第 1 个义项：身体摆放的样子）；句意是：坐的时候要背挺直、姿势放松。画面里能看到的物件有琴凳、琴键和学生的背包带。

pos.zh: 名词：姿势；姿态；立场；态度
动词：故作姿态；装样子

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「姿势的；体位的」
由动词加 -ing 名词化构成，义为「装腔作势；摆姿态」
由动词加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「装腔作势的人」

senses.title: The way the body is held
senses.definition: the position in which someone holds the body when standing, sitting, or walking
senses.definitionCN: 人站立、坐着或行走时身体摆放的位置和样子
senses.example: Poor posture can cause back pain.
senses.exampleCN: 不良姿势会引起背痛。
senses.why: The Latin source meant the placing or setting of something, so the body itself is treated as something set into position.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义是「放置、摆放」，把它用在身体上，身体就像被摆好的一件东西，于是有了姿势、体态。

senses.title: An outward attitude or stance
senses.definition: the attitude or position that a person, group, or country shows toward an issue
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团体或国家对某个问题表现出的态度或立场
senses.example: The government adopted a tougher posture on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在贸易问题上采取了更强硬的立场。
senses.why: A standing posture shows how a body faces the world, so the same word covers how a group faces an issue.
senses.whyCN: 站立的姿态决定身体朝向世界的方向，于是同一个词也用来形容一个团体面对某件事时的朝向，即立场。

senses.title: Behaviour put on for show
senses.definition: behaviour that is deliberately put on to impress others rather than coming naturally
senses.definitionCN: 为了给人好印象而刻意做出来的、并不自然的行为
senses.example: The speech was pure posture rather than a real plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲只是在装样子，并不是真正的计划。
senses.why: When attention moves from the body to the display, a posture becomes something struck for an audience, not lived.
senses.whyCN: 当注意点从身体本身转到「摆给人看」上，姿势就变成了为观众摆出的做派，而非真心情态。

senses.title: The body position of an animal
senses.definition: the resting or ready stance of an animal when it is at rest, on guard, or preparing to act
senses.definitionCN: 动物休息、戒备或准备行动时身体所处的姿态
senses.example: The cat lowered itself into a hunting posture.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫压低身体，摆出捕猎的姿态。
senses.why: If any body can be set into position, an animal body qualifies just as well, with extra shades of readiness.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何身体都能被「摆到位」，动物也一样，而且还多了一层「随时准备行动」的意味。

senses.title: To strike an attitude
senses.definition: to behave in a way that is meant to look impressive or to attract attention
senses.definitionCN: 为了显得了不起或吸引注意而刻意表现
senses.example: Politicians postured for the cameras outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 政客们在大厅外对着镜头摆姿态。
senses.why: The noun sense of showy behaviour turns into a verb that names the very act of posing.
senses.whyCN: 名词中「装样子」的意思转成了动词，直接表示「摆出做派」这个动作本身。

intro.en: Posture comes from Latin ponere, to place, through the noun positura, a placing or position.
intro.cn: posture 来自拉丁语 ponere（放置），经由名词 positura（摆放、位置）进入法语和英语。

items.en: Ponere means to put or place something in position.
items.cn: ponere 意为把某物放置、摆到位。

items.en: Positura means a placing, and also the position that results.
items.cn: positura 意为「摆放」，也指摆放之后形成的位置。

items.en: Posture carries the noun into French as shape or bearing.
items.cn: 古法语以 posture 承接该名词，指外形或举止。

items.en: Posture is first used of the attitude of the body.
items.cn: 英语中的 posture 最早用于描述身体的姿态。

items.en: The word widens to mean a mental or political attitude.
items.cn: 十七到十八世纪，词义扩展到心理或政治上的立场。

items.en: Health writing and politics both keep the word busy.
items.cn: 现代英语里，健康话题与政治评论都在大量使用这个词。

note.en: Posture overlaps with pose and bearing in form, and with stance and attitude in meaning.
note.cn: posture 在形式上与 pose、bearing 相近，在意义上则与 stance、attitude 重合。

entries.definition: relating to the position of the body
entries.definitionCN: 姿势的；体位的，由posture加词尾构成

entries.definition: behaviour that is put on for show
entries.definitionCN: 装腔作势；摆姿态，由动词变形名词化而来

entries.definition: to put up a notice or to send someone to a place
entries.definitionCN: 张贴；派驻，与posture同源于拉丁语「放置」

entries.definition: a particular position of the body, often held for a picture
entries.definitionCN: 姿态：常为拍照而摆出的身体位置

entries.definition: the way a person stands and carries themselves
entries.definitionCN: 举止、仪态：一个人站立与行动的样子

entries.definition: an opinion stated publicly on an issue
entries.definitionCN: 立场：就某问题公开表明的看法

normalIntro.en: Posture is about placing: the body placed straight, or a group placed in a fixed attitude.
normalIntro.cn: posture 的核心是「摆放」：身体被摆正，或者一个团体被摆出固定的态度。

normal.en: Posture and position share the Latin idea of placing.
normal.cn: posture 与 position 共享拉丁语「放置」这一层意思。

normal.en: Postural muscles hold the spine in line.
normal.cn: postural 肌肉作用是把脊椎维持在一条线上。

normal.en: A defensive posture is the body or state standing as if ready for attack.
normal.cn: 防御姿态就是身体或国家摆出随时准备应战的样子。

normal.en: Posturing means posing for an audience rather than acting.
normal.cn: posturing 意为对着观众摆架子，而不是真的行动。

normal.en: Bearing describes the whole carriage, while posture often names the measurable alignment.
normal.cn: bearing 描述整体的举止风度，posture 更常指可以测量的身体对齐方式。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of blocks being straightened so the tower stops leaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞积木被重新摆正，倾斜的塔终于立稳。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole delegation turning to face a single question.
abstract.cn: 想象整个代表团齐刷刷转向同一个问题。

abstract.en: See a man posing in front of a camera while doing nothing real.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在镜头前摆姿势，实则什么也没做。

examples.en: She corrected her posture before the long lesson began.
examples.cn: 长课上到一半前，她先纠正了自己的姿势。

examples.en: Their military posture worried neighbouring countries.
examples.cn: 他们的军事姿态让邻国感到不安。

examples.en: Critics dismissed the announcement as mere posturing.
examples.cn: 批评者认为那项声明只是在装腔作势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破石头」——把弯背像一块歪着的破石头那样摆正，就站出了好姿势；这只是读音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ponere（放置）→ positura（摆放；位置）→ 古法语 posture → 英语 posture，核心义「把东西摆到位」。

sensesIntro.en: Posture begins with the literal placing of the body, extends to the stance of animals and of whole governments, and ends with the emptied-out show of an attitude.
sensesIntro.cn: posture 从身体被「摆到位」出发，扩展到动物体位乃至政府立场，最后落到徒有其表的装腔作势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body set upright, all its parts in their places.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被摆直的身体，各部分都在位。

branches.en: The body placed in position is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 身体被摆到位，是最本义的物理义项。

branches.en: A group facing an issue takes up a stance.
branches.cn: 一个团体面对问题时摆出的朝向，就是立场。

branches.en: The display of an attitude becomes posing and the posture verb.
branches.cn: 把态度拿来展示，就成了作态以及相应的动词。

branches.en: Animal readiness reuses the same body-position frame.
branches.cn: 动物的临战准备沿用了同一套身体位置框架。

branches.en: Good carriage read naturally versus an attitude struck for effect.
branches.cn: 自然的良好体态与刻意做给人的派头形成对照。

intro.en: Posture comes from the Latin placing root ponere, with the pos- stem seen in postural, posture, and position.
intro.cn: posture 来自拉丁语表示「放置」的 ponere，pos- 这个词干出现在 postural、posture、position 之中。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere means to place, and positura means a placing or position.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，positura 意为摆放或位置。

items.example: Ponere gives the placing image.
items.exampleCN: ponere 提供「摆放」的意象。

items.example: Positura is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: positura 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Posture keeps the body-position sense.
items.exampleCN: posture 保留了身体位置的这一层意思。

items.example: The suffix -al forms postural.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 postural。

items.example: Postural exercises help the spine.
items.exampleCN: postural 训练对脊椎有帮助。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms posturing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 posturing。

items.example: Posturing empties the word of its health sense.
items.exampleCN: posturing 让这个词失去了健康层的含义。

items.example: Position shares the placing root.
items.exampleCN: position 共享「放置」词根。

items.example: Compose builds on the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: compose 建立自同一个拉丁动词。

definition_zh: 效力；药力；力量；影响力；潜能；（生物学的）生殖能力
definition_en: the strength of an effect, especially of a drug, a force, or an argument, and also the capacity to produce a result
core_image: 一只握着钥匙的手，钥匙能开多大的锁，取决于它有多合齿
scene: 实验室里，研究员把溶液一再稀释，只为测出它到底能有多强的效力。Even at a tiny dose, the new drug showed remarkable potency in trials.
sceneCN: 这里 potency 是「效力、药力」（第 1 个义项：药物作用的强弱程度）；句意是：即使剂量极小，这种新药在试验中也显示出惊人的效力。场景里出现的物件有移液枪、试管架和记录本。

pos.zh: 名词：效力；力量；影响力；潜能

derivatives.zh: 由本词对应的形容词构成，义为「强有力的；有效的」
由形容词 potent 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「强有力地」
由本词加动词词尾 -ate 构成，义为「增强……的作用」
由动词 potentiate 加 -ion 构成，义为「增效作用」

senses.title: The strength of a drug or substance
senses.definition: the strength of the effect that a drug, chemical, or substance produces at a given dose
senses.definitionCN: 药物、化学物质在给定剂量下所产生作用的强弱程度
senses.example: The potency of the medicine was tested on animals first.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药先是在动物身上测试了药力。
senses.why: The Latin source meant being able, so a drug with potency is a thing that can do a great deal inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义是「能、有力」，所以有 potency 的药就是在体内能做出大事的东西，于是核心意象落成「有多能打」。

senses.title: General power to affect people or events
senses.definition: the general power of something to influence people, events, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 某物影响人、事件或观念的普遍力量
senses.example: Few songs match the potency of that old protest ballad.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有歌能比得上那首老抗议民谣的影响力。
senses.why: Once the can-do idea leaves the body, it names any force that acts on minds and events.
senses.whyCN: 「能做」的意思一旦离开身体，就可以指任何作用于人心和事件的力量。

senses.title: Hidden capacity to develop
senses.definition: the quality of being able to grow or produce an effect later, even if nothing is visible yet
senses.definitionCN: 目前尚未显现、但日后能够成长或起作用的潜在能力
senses.example: The plain room still held a strange potency for her.
senses.exampleCN: 那个朴素的房间对她仍有一种莫名的潜在力量。
senses.why: Able can mean able-to-come, so the same word marks what is only a possibility at the moment.
senses.whyCN: 「能」也可以指「将来能」，于是同一个词转而标注此刻还只是可能性的东西。

senses.title: The force of an argument
senses.definition: the convincing strength of an argument, image, or piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 论证、意象或文字令人信服的力量
senses.example: The report lost much of its potency after errors surfaced.
senses.exampleCN: 错误曝光后，那份报告的说服力大打折扣。
senses.why: If words can move people, they can be weighed by how strongly they act, just like a dose.
senses.whyCN: 如果文字能打动人，就可以像剂量一样被衡量强弱，语言于是也有了与自己相配的效力。

senses.title: Biological power to reproduce
senses.definition: the ability of an organism to reproduce or to perform sexually
senses.definitionCN: 生物繁衍后代或进行性行为的能力
senses.example: Pollution lowered the potency of the male fish in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 污染使那条河里的雄鱼生殖能力下降。
senses.why: Fertility is the oldest setting of able-to-do, so this sense stays close to the Latin root.
senses.whyCN: 繁衍是最古老的「能做」，所以这一义项最贴近拉丁语词根，至今仍保留在生物学的正式说法里。

intro.en: Potency comes from Latin posse, to be able, through potentia, power or ability.
intro.cn: potency 来自拉丁语 posse（能够），经由 potentia（力量、能力）进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning master or husband underlies the family, though the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，该词族源自一个表示「主人、丈夫」的原始印欧语重构形式，但这一重构存在不确定性。

items.en: Posse means to be able, and potentia means power.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，potentia 意为「力量」。

items.en: Potentia names official power and also an inborn capacity.
items.cn: potentia 既指公权力，也指与生俱来的能力。

items.en: Potence arrives from French alongside the Latinized potentia.
items.cn: 法语写法 potence 与拉丁化的 potentia 先后传入，而后者的形式占了上风。

items.en: The word is used for the power of medicines and then of states.
items.cn: 这一时期的英语先用它表示药力，随后也用于国家的实力。

items.en: Pharmacology and social science adapt the word to their own measures.
items.cn: 现代的药理学与社会科学把这词纳入了各自的度量体系。

note.en: Potency keeps the potent family around it, and overlaps with power, force, and efficacy in meaning.
note.cn: potency 身边是 potent 一家人，意义上则与 power、force、efficacy 相互重叠。

entries.definition: having great power or effect
entries.definitionCN: 强有力的；有效的

entries.definition: a ruler with great power
entries.definitionCN: 君主；掌权者，与potency同源于「有力量」

entries.definition: possible but not yet actual
entries.definitionCN: 潜在的；可能的，以「能够」为共同词根

entries.definition: the ability to act or control others
entries.definitionCN: 力量；权力：行动或掌控他人的能力

entries.definition: physical strength or strong pressure
entries.definitionCN: 力；威力：物理上的力量或强烈的冲击

entries.definition: the ability to produce the intended result
entries.definitionCN: 功效：产生预期效果的能力

normalIntro.en: Potency is the noun of able: how much something can do, once it is measured.
normalIntro.cn: potency 是「能」的名词形式：一件事一旦被衡量，就是它能做多大。

normal.en: Potency is the noun of potent, and both reach back to Latin posse, to be able.
normal.cn: potency 是 potent 的名词，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 posse（能够）。

normal.en: A high potency drug needs a very small dose.
normal.cn: 高效力的药只需要很小的剂量。

normal.en: Potential and potentate share the same able root.
normal.cn: potential 与 potentate 共享同一个「能够」词根。

normal.en: In biology, potency can mean the ability to reproduce.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，potency 可以指生殖能力。

normal.en: Do not confuse potency with potence, a rarer French-flavoured spelling.
normal.cn: 别把 potency 与更罕见、带法语色彩的写法 potence 混为一谈。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a key, each turn of the key deciding how much the lock can do.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握住钥匙，每次转动都决定锁最终能起多大作用。

abstract.en: Imagine an old ballad that makes a crowded room go silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一首老民谣让满屋子的人一下子安静下来。

abstract.en: See an unopened seed in a plain pot, doing nothing yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只朴素花盆里未破土的种子，此刻还什么也没做。

examples.en: The drug lost its potency after sitting in the sun.
examples.cn: 那药在太阳下放了一阵后就失效了。

examples.en: The potency of his arguments silenced the room.
examples.cn: 他论点的说服力让满屋人都沉默下来。

examples.en: Chemists measured the potency of each sample.
examples.cn: 化学家逐一测量了每个样本的效力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡腾」——泡腾片一进水就能轰地冒出力量，这正是效力的画面；这只是读音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）→ potentia（力量、能力）→ 法语 potence → 英语 potency，核心义「有多能做」。

sensesIntro.en: Potency always asks how much something can do: on a body, on events, in the future, in an argument, or in passing on life.
sensesIntro.cn: potency 始终在问一件事能有多大作为：对身体的效力、对事件的力量、将来的潜能、论证的说服力，以及传续生命的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning a key that opens exactly as much as it can reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手转动钥匙，钥匙能开到多远，全看它有多合齿。

branches.en: How strongly a substance acts is the measured physical sense.
branches.cn: 物质作用有多强，是可测量的物理义项。

branches.en: Influence on people and events is the generalised sense.
branches.cn: 对人与事件的影响，是该词泛化后的义项。

branches.en: Capacity kept in reserve is the latent sense.
branches.cn: 被存起来以备将来的能力，是潜能这一义项。

branches.en: An argument rated by its force borrows the dose image.
branches.cn: 论证按强弱来评定，借用了剂量的那层比喻。

branches.en: The oldest able sense stays in biology.
branches.cn: 最古老的「能够」之义，今天仍保留在生物学里。

intro.en: Potency belongs to a Latin family built on posse, able, which also gives potent, potential, and potentate.
intro.cn: potency 属于以拉丁语 posse（能够）为核心的一族词，同族还有 potent、potential、potentate。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse, to be able, yields potens, powerful, and potentia, power.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse（能够）派生出 potens（有力量的）与 potentia（力量）。

items.example: Posse is the deepest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: posse 是这个词族最深的一层词根。

items.example: Potentia is the direct ancestor of the noun.
items.exampleCN: potentia 是这个名词的直接祖先。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ency forms potency.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ency 构成 potency。

items.example: Potency keeps the noun pattern.
items.exampleCN: potency 保留了这一名词形式。

items.example: Potent is the adjective behind potency.
items.exampleCN: potent 是 potency 背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms potently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 potently。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms potentiate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 potentiate。

items.example: Potential shares the able root.
items.exampleCN: potential 共享「能够」词根。

items.example: Potentate narrows power to a person.
items.exampleCN: potentate 把「力量」收窄到指某个人。

definition_zh: 有力的；有说服力的；强效的；（男性）有性能力的
definition_en: having great power, force, or effect
core_image: 一个小小的药瓶，里面的药力却让整只手都微微发紧
scene: 发言者没讲长篇，只放出一张旧照片，全场突然安静。That single photograph proved a potent reminder of the disaster.
sceneCN: 这里 potent 是「有说服力的力量」（第 1 个义项：能产生强烈作用）；句意：那记提问落得太重，整个会场霎时安静。

pos.zh: 有力的；有影响力的；有说服力的
强效的；效力强的

derivatives.zh: potent 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「力量；效力；潜势」
potent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有力地；极具效力地」
potent 加否定前缀 im- 构成，义为「无力的；无能为力的」
由 potency 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「增强……的作用、使增效」（科学用语）

senses.title: Having great physical or natural power
senses.definition: able to produce a strong physical or natural effect
senses.definitionCN: 能够产生强烈的物理或自然作用的
senses.example: The river becomes a potent force after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨过后，这条河变成一股强大的力量。
senses.why: The word descends from Latin posse, to be able, so potent first names raw power that can act and get things done.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语 posse（能够），所以 potent 首先指那种真能行动起来、起作用的原始力量。

senses.title: Strong in persuasion or influence
senses.titleCN: 有说服力的；影响巨大的
senses.definition: so strong in language or logic that people are hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 言辞或逻辑强到令人难以抗拒的
senses.example: Her closing remarks were a potent argument for reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她的结束语是支持改革的一个有力论证。
senses.why: The same power is abstracted from bodies to words and ideas, so a potent argument is one that can move minds.
senses.whyCN: 同一股力量从身体抽离到言辞与观念上，所以「有力的论证」就是能推动人心的论证。

senses.title: Strong in medical effect
senses.definition: having a very strong effect as a medicine or drug
senses.definitionCN: 作为药物时效力很强的
senses.example: This is a potent drug, so take only the prescribed dose.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一种强效药，因此只按处方剂量服用。
senses.why: Medicine shows power at the smallest scale: a few drops of a potent drug can change the whole body.
senses.whyCN: 药物把小尺度上的力量显示得最清楚：几滴强效药就能改变整个身体。

senses.title: Sexually able, of a male
senses.definition: sexually able, used of a man
senses.definitionCN: 有性能力的，用于男性
senses.example: Older texts described the young bull as sexually potent.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的文献把那头小公牛描述为性能力旺盛。
senses.why: Producing or driving life was the earliest sense of power, so potent was applied to reproductive ability before it turned technical.
senses.whyCN: 在最早的观念里，能生育、能繁衍就是力量，所以 potent 最初也用于生殖能力，后来这一义项才变得专门化。

intro.en: Potent comes from Latin potens, powerful, the present participle of posse, to be able.
intro.cn: potent 来自拉丁语 potens（有力量的），是 posse（能够）的现在分词。

items.en: Posse, to be able, gives the participle potens, able or powerful.
items.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够，其分词 potens 意为有能力的、有力量的。

items.en: Potentia, power or capacity, is the noun drawn from the same participle.
items.cn: 同源名词 potentia 意为「力量、能力」。

items.en: Old French and Anglo-French carry potent into the legal and medical usage of medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语与英法法语把 potent 带入中世纪欧洲的法律与医学用法。

items.en: Potent enters written English describing strength of arms and of remedies.
items.cn: potent 约在十五世纪进入英语文献，用来形容武力与药效。

items.en: The adjective widens to arguments, symbols, ideas, and chemical or biological agents.
items.cn: 到了现代英语，这个形容词扩展到论证、象征、观念以及化学或生物制剂。

note.en: Potent is the adjective of raw ability, close to its own family and to the wider set of power words.
note.cn: potent 是表示「真能起作用」的形容词，与自家词族相邻，也处在更广的力量词汇群里。

entries.definition: the power or strength something has
entries.definitionCN: 效力；力量；潜势

entries.definition: without power to act or change things
entries.definitionCN: 无力的；无能为力的

entries.definition: possible but not yet actual
entries.definitionCN: 潜在的；可能的

entries.definition: a sign of something about to happen
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近、词源不同：词首为 port-，意为「预兆」。

entries.definition: having a lot of strength or influence
entries.definitionCN: 强大的；有影响力的（最通用的说法）

entries.definition: physically fit or able to resist force
entries.definitionCN: 强壮的；坚固的（偏身体与材质）

entries.definition: producing the wanted result
entries.definitionCN: 有效的（重在结果，而非力量大小）

normalIntro.en: Potent is the adjective of posse, to be able: something potent can really do work in the world.
normalIntro.cn: potent 来自表示「能够」的 posse，也就是「真能在世上起作用」的形容词。

normal.en: Potency is the noun: the drug lost its potency on the shelf.
normal.cn: potency 是它的名词：那药物在货架上放久了失效了。

normal.en: The prefix in- before a p sounds as im-, so potent pairs with impotent.
normal.cn: 源自 in- 的否定前缀遇 p 时写作 im-，所以 potent 的反义是 impotent。

normal.en: Latin posse means to be able, and it also gives possible and possibility.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够，它也派生出 possible 和 possibility。

normal.en: A potent drug works in tiny doses; a potent argument works in few words.
normal.cn: 强效药只需极小剂量，有力的论证也只需寥寥数语。

normal.en: Compare portent: one letter apart, but portent means an omen.
normal.cn: 对比 portent：只差一个字母，但 portent 意思是预兆。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop of medicine that makes a whole arm tremble.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴药水就让整条手臂微微发抖。

abstract.en: Imagine one short sentence that silences a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象一句简短的话让整间屋子安静下来。

abstract.en: Think of a tap on a drum that fills a whole hall with sound.
abstract.cn: 想象鼓面上轻轻一击，就让整个大厅充满声音。

examples.en: The speech was a potent reminder of why the rules matter.
examples.cn: 这场演讲有力地提醒了人们为什么这些规则重要。

examples.en: Doctors warn that this is a potent drug and must be used carefully.
examples.cn: 医生提醒这是一种强效药，必须谨慎使用。

examples.en: The two ideas formed a potent combination for the campaign.
examples.cn: 这两个观念构成了这场运动的有力组合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「怕疼」——药力太强，喝下去让人直呼怕疼；这只是谐音联想，与 posse 的词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）+ 现在分词词尾 -ens → potens（有力量的）→ 古法语 → 英语 potent，核心义「真能起作用的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Potent starts as raw power that can act, then moves to the power of words, then to the strength of medicine, and finally to a narrow sense about male reproductive ability.
sensesIntro.cn: potent 先指能行动起来的原始力量，再指言辞或论证的力量，然后指药物的效力，最后收窄为关于男性生殖能力的专义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny dose that still fills the body with force.
core.cn: 核心意象：极小的一剂，却让全身都感到力量。

branches.en: Raw power of bodies and nature is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 身体与自然界的原始力量是基本义项。

branches.en: Power moved into words and arguments is the abstract sense.
branches.cn: 力量转移到言辞与论证上，就是抽象义项。

branches.en: A potent drug shows the strongest effect at the smallest size.
branches.cn: 强效药以最小的体量显示出最强的效果。

branches.en: The reproductive sense is an old, narrow label for a man.
branches.cn: 生殖义项是较早、范围较窄的用法，专指男性。

branches.en: Both a flood and a strong medicine are potent because effect far exceeds size.
branches.cn: 洪水与强效药之所以 potent，都是因为效果远远超出体量。

intro.en: Potent is a Latin participle turned adjective, and English builds potency, potently, and impotent around it.
intro.cn: potent 是拉丁语分词转成的形容词，英语围绕它构成 potency、potently 与 impotent。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse means to be able, and its participle potens gives both the adjective and the noun potentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够，其分词 potens 同时派生出形容词与名词 potentia。

items.example: Posse supplies the idea of ability behind potent.
items.exampleCN: posse 为 potent 提供了「有能力」这一层含义。

items.example: Potens is the participle that became the adjective.
items.exampleCN: potens 是后来变成形容词的分词。

items.example: Potent keeps the participle meaning.
items.exampleCN: potent 保留了分词的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix forms potency from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由同一词干构成 potency。

items.example: Potency names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: potency 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix makes the adverb potently.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成副词 potently。

items.example: Before p the prefix becomes im-, giving impotent.
items.exampleCN: 遇 p 时否定前缀写作 im-，构成 impotent。

items.example: Impotent reverses the core idea of power.
items.exampleCN: impotent 把核心的「力量」整个反转。

items.meaningCN: 表示使……、使成为的动词后缀
items.example: The suffix forms the technical verb potentiate.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成科技术语动词 potentiate。

items.example: Potentiate is used in pharmacology.
items.exampleCN: potentiate 常用于药理学。

definition_en: birds such as chickens, ducks, and turkeys kept for their meat or eggs
core_image: 农家院里的鸡舍，母鸡咯咯叫着，笼子里挤满待宰的幼禽
scene: 农场主说，这批货要在天亮前装箱送到城里的市场。The farm sells poultry to butcher shops across the city.
sceneCN: 这里 poultry 是「家禽」（第 1 个义项：饲养供食用的禽类）；句意：这家农场把家禽卖给全城的肉店。

pos.zh: 家禽（总称，不可数）
禽肉（供食用的家禽肉）

derivatives.zh: 由 poultry 的旧式词干加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「家禽商；卖禽肉的人」
poultry 去掉后缀后的词干名词，义为「雏禽；幼鸡幼火鸡」
复合词：poultry + man，义为「家禽饲养者；养禽工人」

senses.title: Domestic birds kept for food
senses.definition: birds such as chickens, ducks, geese, and turkeys that are kept on farms for their meat or eggs
senses.definitionCN: 在农场饲养、供肉用或蛋用的鸡、鸭、鹅、火鸡一类鸟
senses.example: The village keeps poultry in a fenced yard behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 村里人在屋后的围栏里养家禽。
senses.why: The French root poulet meant a young fowl, and the collective use lumps all farmed birds under one word.
senses.whyCN: 法语词根 poulet 本指幼禽，而集合用法把所有家养的禽鸟归到同一个词下。

senses.title: The meat of these birds
senses.definition: the meat from these birds, sold and cooked as food
senses.definitionCN: 来自这些禽鸟的肉，作为食物出售与烹饪
senses.example: Wash your hands after handling raw poultry and eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 处理生禽肉和鸡蛋后要洗手。
senses.why: When the animal becomes food on a menu, the same collective noun shifts from the bird to its meat.
senses.whyCN: 当动物变成菜单上的食物时，同一个集合名词就从「鸟」转向「鸟肉」。

senses.title: Farming as an industry
senses.definition: the business of breeding and raising these birds for sale
senses.definitionCN: 繁育与饲养这些鸟以供出售的行业
senses.example: Poultry is one of the fastest growing farm sectors.
senses.exampleCN: 家禽业是增长最快的农业部门之一。
senses.why: A collective noun naturally stands for the whole trade once the birds are produced at industrial scale.
senses.whyCN: 当禽类按工业规模生产时，集合名词自然就代表整个行业。

intro.en: Poultry comes from Old French pouletrie, the trade in fowls, from poulet, a young fowl, from Latin pullus.
intro.cn: poultry 来自古法语 pouletrie（禽类买卖），源自 poulet（幼禽），再上溯到拉丁语 pullus。

items.en: Pullus means a young animal, especially a young bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pullus 意为幼兽，尤指幼鸟。

items.en: Poulet, a young fowl, and pouletrie, the business and stock of fowls, appear first in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语先出现 poulet（幼禽）与 pouletrie（家禽买卖与存货）。

items.en: Pultry fills a legal roll about the sale of birds in medieval London.
items.cn: 十四世纪伦敦一份关于鸟类买卖的法律卷宗里已见 pultry。

items.en: Poultry spreads through market documents, where it means fowls sold as food.
items.cn: poultry 经市场文书在英语里传播开来，指作为食物出售的禽鸟。

items.en: Modern English uses poultry for the birds and their meat, and builds a whole farming industry on the word.
items.cn: 现代英语用 poultry 兼指家禽及其肉，并围绕它建起整个养殖产业。

note.en: Poultry is a French-derived collective noun, close in form to its older stem poult and in meaning to fowl and livestock.
note.cn: poultry 是源自法语的集合名词，外形上连着较早的词干 poult，意义上与 fowl、livestock 相邻。

entries.definition: a young turkey or young fowl
entries.definitionCN: 同根词：雏禽、小火鸡

entries.definition: a person who sells poultry
entries.definitionCN: 家禽商；卖禽肉的人

entries.definition: a young hen
entries.definitionCN: 小母鸡（同为拉丁 pullus 的后裔）

entries.definition: very small and of little value
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近、词源不同：意为「微不足道的」。

entries.definition: a bird kept for its meat or eggs
entries.definitionCN: 家禽（较古雅或指野禽的统称）

entries.definition: farm animals kept for use or profit
entries.definitionCN: 牲畜（上位概念，禽类可含其中）

entries.definition: a farm that raises poultry
entries.definitionCN: 禽场；家禽饲养场

normalIntro.en: Poultry keeps the French bird word: poulet means chicken, and the trade in such birds became poultry.
normalIntro.cn: poultry 保留了法语的「鸟」词：poulet 意为鸡，买卖这类禽鸟的生意就成了 poultry。

normal.en: Poultry is uncountable: say some poultry, never a poultry.
normal.cn: poultry 是不可数集合名词：说 some poultry，不能说 a poultry。

normal.en: It covers birds and meat alike, much like the word fish.
normal.cn: 它既指禽也指禽肉，和 fish 的用法相似。

normal.en: A person who sells poultry is a poulterer.
normal.cn: 卖家禽的人叫 poulterer。

normal.en: The stem poult, a young fowl, also names a young turkey: a turkey poult.
normal.cn: 词干 poult 指幼禽，turkey poult 就是小火鸡。

normal.en: Industry names follow the same pattern: poultry farm, poultry industry.
normal.cn: 行业搭配遵循同一模式：poultry farm、poultry industry。

abstract.en: Picture a sunlit yard of hens and ducks all under one word.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光下满是鸡鸭的院子，被一个词统摄。

abstract.en: Hear the first syllable like the French word for chicken, poulet.
abstract.cn: 把开头音听成法语的鸡 poulet。

abstract.en: Think of a delivery van marked with the word poultry, driving from farm to market.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆印着 poultry 的货车从农场开往市场。

examples.en: The farm raises poultry and sells eggs locally.
examples.cn: 这个农场饲养家禽，并在本地出售鸡蛋。

examples.en: Poultry prices rose sharply because of the disease.
examples.cn: 由于这种疾病，禽肉价格大幅上涨。

examples.en: Keep raw poultry away from cooked food.
examples.cn: 生禽肉要与熟食分开存放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「剖了退」——家禽先「剖」再上桌，卖不掉的就「退」回去；这是谐音联想，与法语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pullus（幼禽）+ 法语集合后缀 -trie → 古法语 pouletrie（禽类买卖）→ 英语 poultry，核心义「圈养供食用的禽鸟」。

sensesIntro.en: Poultry begins as a word for fowls kept for food, extends to the meat of those birds, and by extension covers the whole farming business.
sensesIntro.cn: poultry 起初指饲养供食用的禽鸟，再延伸到这些鸟的肉，最后扩及整个养殖行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded farmyard of hens and ducks and their meat on a plate.
core.cn: 核心意象：挤满鸡鸭的农家院子，以及盘中它们的肉。

branches.en: Farmed birds as animals form the first sense.
branches.cn: 作为动物的家禽构成第一个义项。

branches.en: The same birds on a plate give the meat sense.
branches.cn: 同样这些鸟在餐盘上，就产生禽肉义项。

branches.en: Organized breeding turns the birds into an industry.
branches.cn: 有组织的繁育把家禽变成一门行业。

branches.en: Birds and trade join when the word describes a growing sector.
branches.cn: 当这个词描述一个成长中的部门时，「禽」与「业」结合在一起。

branches.en: Bird and meat share one word the way fish and fish do in English.
branches.cn: 在英语里，禽与禽肉共用一个词，正如和鱼相关的说法。

intro.en: Poultry is a French collective noun, and English builds poult, poulterer, and poultryman from the same bird word.
intro.cn: poultry 是法语集合名词，英语用同一个「鸟」词构成 poult、poulterer 与 poultryman。

latinIntro.en: Latin pullus, a young bird, heads the family; the French forms poulet and pouletrie are its descendants.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pullus（幼禽）是这一族的源头，法语 poulet 与 pouletrie 都是它的后裔。

items.example: Pullus is the deep source of the family.
items.exampleCN: pullus 是这一词族的最初源头。

items.example: Poulet is the everyday French word for chicken.
items.exampleCN: poulet 是法语里日常的「鸡」。

items.example: The trade noun is the direct parent of poultry.
items.exampleCN: 这个「买卖」名词是 poultry 的直接母体。

items.example: Poultry keeps the collective sense.
items.exampleCN: poultry 保留了集合含义。

items.example: Poult is the bare stem in modern English.
items.exampleCN: poult 是现代英语里的裸露词干。

items.meaningCN: 表示从事某事之人的后缀
items.example: The suffix makes the seller word poulterer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成「卖禽者」poulterer。

items.example: Poulterer keeps the older stem poult.
items.exampleCN: poulterer 保留了较早的词干 poult。

items.meaning: a person who works at something
items.meaningCN: 从事某业者的构词成分
items.example: The combining form gives poultryman.
items.exampleCN: 这一构词成分构成 poultryman。

items.example: Poultryman joins the bird word to a worker word.
items.exampleCN: poultryman 把「禽」与「从业者」拼在一起。

definition_zh: 务实的；注重实际的；实用主义的
definition_en: dealing with problems in a practical way rather than by theory or fixed ideas
core_image: 卷起袖子先干起来的人，把漂亮方案折成能用的纸盒
scene: 预算被砍了一半，团队不再争论理想方案，而是挑出明天就能落地的一条。The manager took a pragmatic view and picked the cheapest fix.
sceneCN: 这里 pragmatic 是「务实的」（第 1 个义项：按实际情况办事、不讲空头理论）；句意：经理从实际出发，选了最省钱的解决办法。

pos.zh: 务实的；讲究实际的；实用主义的
（语言研究）语用的

derivatives.zh: pragmatic 去尾换 -ism 构成，义为「务实作风；实用主义」
pragmatic 换 -ist 后缀构成，义为「务实者；实用主义者」
pragmatic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「从实际出发地」
希腊语词干 pragmat- 经拉丁语进入英语，义为「事、实务」（多见于哲学术语中）

senses.title: Dealing with things practically
senses.definition: solving problems by what works in real conditions rather than by theory or principle
senses.definitionCN: 依据现实条件下什么行得通来解决问题，而非依据理论或原则
senses.example: We need a pragmatic plan, not a perfect one.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要的是可行的计划，而不是完美的计划。
senses.why: The Greek root pragma means a deed or thing done, so the adjective asks what action actually delivers results.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 pragma 意为「行为、做成的事」，因此这个形容词关心的是哪种行动真能出结果。

senses.title: Politically flexible, not doctrinaire
senses.definition: willing to compromise on ideology in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达成结果而愿意在意识形态上妥协的
senses.example: She is too pragmatic to defend a policy that clearly fails.
senses.exampleCN: 她太务实了，不会去维护一项明显失败的政策。
senses.why: When the practical idea enters politics, it becomes the label for leaders who trade principle for outcome.
senses.whyCN: 当「务实」进入政治语境，它就用来形容那些以原则换结果的政治人物。

senses.title: Related to language use in context
senses.definition: relating to the way language is used in real situations and what speakers mean
senses.definitionCN: 研究语言在真实情境中如何使用以及说话人真实意图的
senses.example: The paper takes a pragmatic view of face-to-face requests.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文从语用角度考察面对面请求。
senses.why: Language study borrows the word for how meanings are actually used in context, the same act-over-ideal logic.
senses.whyCN: 语言学研究借用这个词来表示「意义在语境中实际如何使用」，与「看行动而非理想」的逻辑一致。

intro.en: Pragmatic comes from Greek pragmatikos, fit for business, from pragma, a deed, through Latin pragmaticus.
intro.cn: pragmatic 来自希腊语 pragmatikos（适合办事的），源出 pragma（行为、事），经拉丁语 pragmaticus 传入。

items.en: Pragma means a deed, an act, or a matter, from prassein, to do.
items.cn: 希腊语 pragma 意为「行为、行动、事务」，源自动词 prassein（做）。

items.en: Pragmatikos means fit for action or skilled in business.
items.cn: pragmatikos 意为「适合行动的、擅长办事的」。

items.en: Pragmaticus enters Latin and names a person skilled in practical affairs or law.
items.cn: pragmaticus 进入拉丁语，指精通实务或法律的人。

items.en: Legal and imperial language fixes pragmatic to rules made for the matter at hand rather than general principle.
items.cn: 法律与帝国文书把 pragmatic 固定为「就事论事下达的」规则，而非依普遍原则。

items.en: Nineteenth-century philosophy gives pragmatic its modern sense of judging ideas by practical results.
items.cn: 十九世纪哲学赋予 pragmatic 现代意义：以实际效果来判断观念。

note.en: Pragmatic is close in form to its noun family and close in meaning to practical, realistic, and utilitarian.
note.cn: pragmatic 外形上连着它的名词词族，意义上与 practical、realistic、utilitarian 相邻。

entries.definition: the habit of judging things by what works
entries.definitionCN: 以效果为标准的作风或哲学主张

entries.definition: a person who cares above all about results
entries.definitionCN: 务实者；实用主义者

entries.definition: certain that one is right and refusing discussion
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写后缀相近、词源不同：词根为 dogma，意为「教条式的」。

entries.definition: concerned with real use rather than theory
entries.definitionCN: 实际的；实用的（最通用的近义词）

entries.definition: accepting how things really are
entries.definitionCN: 现实的；切实的（重在看清现状）

entries.definition: valued only for usefulness
entries.definitionCN: 功利的；以有用性为准的

normalIntro.en: Pragmatic comes from the Greek word for a deed, so it always asks what someone actually does, not what they say.
normalIntro.cn: pragmatic 源自希腊语里表示「行为」的词，因此它总在问「实际做了什么」，而不是「怎么说的」。

normal.en: The noun pragmatism ends in -ism, like other schools of thought.
normal.cn: 名词 pragmatism 以 -ism 结尾，与其它思想流派的构词相同。

normal.en: A pragmatist is a person who wants results, formed with the -ist suffix.
normal.cn: pragmatist 是用 -ist 后缀构成的「想要结果的人」。

normal.en: The adverb is pragmatically, used like practically.
normal.cn: 副词是 pragmatically，用法接近 practically。

normal.en: Learn it with its opposite: a pragmatic decision against a dogmatic one.
normal.cn: 和反义对照记：a pragmatic decision 对应 a dogmatic decision。

normal.en: The core of the word is pragma, a thing done, so keep the image of an action rather than a theory.
normal.cn: 这个词的核心是 pragma（做成的事），所以要记住「行动」而不是「理论」。

abstract.en: Imagine rolling up your sleeves before anyone even finishes describing the problem.
abstract.cn: 想象别人还没把问题说完，你已经挽起袖子开工。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler trading away a corner of principle to save the whole plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一位执政者舍掉一角原则，保住整个计划。

abstract.en: Think of a speaker who means a polite no with a gentle may.
abstract.cn: 想象有人用一句温和的 may 表示委婉的拒绝，这就是语用层面的意思。

examples.en: She took a pragmatic approach and solved it by Friday.
examples.cn: 她采取务实的方法，到周五就解决了。

examples.en: His pragmatic style won votes from both sides.
examples.cn: 他务实的作风为他赢得了双方的选票。

examples.en: The report offers pragmatic advice for small firms.
examples.cn: 这份报告为小公司提供了切合实际的建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑锅买题」——先把锅扑住买上菜，再谈这一题怎么做；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语 pragma 无关。

root: 希腊语 prassein（做）+ 名词词干 pragmat-（做成的事）→ pragmatikos（适合办事的）→ 拉丁语 pragmaticus → 英语 pragmatic，核心义「看实际做成了什么」。

sensesIntro.en: Pragmatic starts as the quality of judging by real results, extends to leaders who bend principle for outcome, and is then borrowed by language study.
sensesIntro.cn: pragmatic 先是「以实际结果为标准」的性质，再指愿为结果变通原则的领导者，最后被语言学研究借用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who acts first and argues later.
core.cn: 核心意象：先动手再做解释的人。

branches.en: Judging by what works is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 按「行不行得通」来判断，是日常义项。

branches.en: The political sense is about giving up doctrine for results.
branches.cn: 政治义项讲的是为结果放弃教条。

branches.en: Language study borrows it for meaning as actually used.
branches.cn: 语言学研究借它表示「实际使用中的意义」。

branches.en: A pragmatic person and a pragmatic politician both trade perfect plans for workable ones.
branches.cn: 务实之人和务实政客都是拿完美方案换可行方案。

branches.en: Both senses ask what something is used for, not what it ideally means.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关心「这东西实际拿去干什么用」，而不只是「理应是什么意思」。

intro.en: The stem pragmat- comes from Greek pragma, a deed, and English adds -ic, -ism, -ist, and the adverb ending to build the family.
intro.cn: 词干 pragmat- 来自希腊语 pragma（行为），英语再加 -ic、-ism、-ist 与副词词尾构成整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek pragma and pragmatikos passed through Latin as pragmaticus, keeping the sense of practical affairs.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 pragma 与 pragmatikos 经拉丁语 pragmaticus 传入，保留了「实务」的含义。

items.example: Prassein gives the sense of doing.
items.exampleCN: prassein 提供「做」这一层意义。

items.example: Pragma is the stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pragma 是整个词族的词干来源。

items.meaningCN: 动作名词的扩展词干成分
items.example: The stem element carries the word into pragmatikos.
items.exampleCN: 这一词干成分把这个词带到 pragmatikos 中。

items.meaningCN: 适合办事的；擅长行动的
items.example: Pragmatikos is the direct ancestor of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: pragmatikos 是这个形容词的直接祖先。

items.example: Pragmaticus carries the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: pragmaticus 把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成英语形容词。

items.example: Pragmatic keeps the practical sense.
items.exampleCN: pragmatic 保留了「讲实际」之义。

items.meaningCN: 表示学说或作风的后缀
items.example: The suffix forms the noun pragmatism.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成名词 pragmatism。

items.example: The suffix forms the person noun pragmatist.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成指人的 pragmatist。

items.example: The suffix forms the adverb pragmatically.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成副词 pragmatically。

latinEntries.meaning: an imperial ruling on a particular matter
latinEntries.meaningCN: 就特定事务作出的敕令

definition_en: a small sea animal with a long body, ten legs and a thin shell, eaten as food
core_image: 煮熟后弯成月牙的一只虾，尾巴贴着头，壳红亮
scene: 夜市的海鲜摊上，炭火把一排虾烤得通红，摊主刷上蒜蓉黄油翻了个面。At the night market the stallholder brushed the prawn with garlic butter and turned it over the coals.
sceneCN: 这里 prawn 是「虾」（第 1 个义项：一种可食用的小型节肢动物）；句意：夜市摊主给那只虾刷上蒜蓉黄油，在炭火上翻了个面。

pos.zh: 虾；大虾；对虾

derivatives.zh: 由 prawn 加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「像虾的；有虾味的」
由 prawn 加后缀 -y 构成，口语中义为「虾味浓的；虾多的」

senses.title: A small ten-footed sea animal
senses.definition: a small sea creature with a long body, a thin shell and ten legs, used as food
senses.definitionCN: 身体细长、壳薄、有十只脚、可食用的小型海洋动物
senses.example: We bought a kilo of fresh prawns at the quay.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在码头买了一公斤新鲜虾。
senses.why: The word is the everyday meat name for the animal itself, the sense a fisherman or a cook reaches for first.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的肉食名称，直指这种动物本体；渔人说 prawn、厨子说 prawn，想到的都是水里那只会弓身弹跳的小东西。

senses.title: A dish of prawns
senses.definition: prawns served as a dish, often peeled, cooked and eaten by the handful
senses.definitionCN: 作为菜肴端上桌的虾，常已去壳烹熟，成把取食
senses.example: The tapas menu lists grilled prawns with lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 塔帕斯菜单上有柠檬烤虾。
senses.why: Once an animal is food, its plural name becomes a dish name, so the menu says prawns where the boat says prawn.
senses.whyCN: 一旦动物成了食物，它的复数形式就顺理成章变成菜名：渔船说的是「虾」，菜单写的是「烤虾」「虾仁拼盘」。

senses.title: A dish cooked in a rich sauce
senses.definition: in Malaysian and Singaporean cooking, a large prawn fried in a thick spicy sauce
senses.definitionCN: 在马来西亚与新加坡菜肴中，指用浓稠香辣酱汁炒成的大虾
senses.example: The chef taught us how to stir-fry a prawn in chilli paste.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师教我们用辣椒酱炒大虾。
senses.why: Regional kitchens made the plain prawn into a signature dish, and the word alone now names that sauce-covered plate.
senses.whyCN: 地方菜系把普通的虾做成招牌菜，于是单说 prawn，在某些餐馆里就特指那盘裹满酱汁、红得发亮的炒虾。

senses.title: Prawn as a nickname for a small person
senses.definition: a teasing nickname for someone short, used rather like shrimp
senses.definitionCN: 对个子矮小的亲昵戏称，用法近似 shrimp
senses.example: His teammates have called him Prawn since school.
senses.exampleCN: 从学生时代起，队友就叫他「小虾」。
senses.why: A prawn is small and curled, so the word slips from the creature to a person, first as a joke.
senses.whyCN: 虾小、蜷、不占地方，词义便从动物滑到人身上，先是玩笑，慢慢变成熟人口中的绰号。

senses.title: To fish for prawns
senses.definition: to catch prawns commercially, usually with fine nets dragged along the seabed
senses.definitionCN: 商业性地捕捞虾，通常用细网在海床上拖过
senses.example: Small boats prawn the estuary at low tide.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时小船在河口捕虾。
senses.why: Out of the noun comes a verb: if prawns are the catch, then to prawn is to go and take them.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词是英语常见路径：虾是渔获，那么 to prawn 就是出海把它捞上来，于是这层意思自然生长出来。

intro.en: Prawn is a Middle English word of uncertain origin, first recorded in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: prawn 是中古英语词，词源不确定，最早见于十四世纪记录。

items.en: Prawn first appears in a list of food fish, spelled prayne or prane.
items.cn: prawn 最初出现在一份食用鱼虾清单中，拼作 prayne 或 prane。
