items.en: Johnson defines the word simply as a shrimp, tying it to the smaller cousin.
items.cn: 约翰逊词典把它简单定义为「shrimp」，把它与小一号的虾联系起来。

items.en: British menus adopt prawn for sea-farmed shrimp, and the word gains a cooking life of its own.
items.cn: 英国菜单用 prawn 指海洋养殖的大虾，这个词因此获得独立的烹饪生命力。

items.en: In Malaysia and Singapore, prawn names a thick sauce-fried dish and is written into menu English.
items.cn: 在马来西亚与新加坡，prawn 指浓酱炒制的虾菜，并被写进当地的菜单英语。

items.en: Prawn extends to aquaculture, to fishing boats, and to a teasing nickname.
items.cn: prawn 进一步扩展到水产养殖、捕虾船与戏谑绰号之上。

note.en: Prawn sits beside the small-shelled seafood words shrimp, krill and crayfish in form, and beside lobster and crab in meaning.
note.cn: prawn 在形式上与小壳海鲜词 shrimp、krill、crayfish 相邻，在意义上与龙虾、蟹同属一类。

entries.definition: a very small sea animal of the same kind, the usual word in North America
entries.definitionCN: 同类但更小的虾，在北美是常用词；与 prawn 常互换，但语域不同

entries.definition: a tiny shrimp-like animal that whales feed on
entries.definitionCN: 鲸类取食的微小虾状甲壳动物（拼写相近，来源不同）

entries.definition: a style of swimming with a low, wide arm stroke
entries.definitionCN: 低而宽的划臂泳姿，因动作像虾而由 prawn 构成的复合词

entries.definition: a large sea animal with a thick shell and big claws, eaten as food
entries.definitionCN: 带厚壳和大钳、可食用的大型海洋动物（龙虾）

entries.definition: a sea animal with a flat shell and claws, that walks sideways
entries.definitionCN: 横行的海洋动物，甲壳扁平、带钳（蟹）

entries.definition: a small lobster-like animal that lives in fresh water
entries.definitionCN: 生活在淡水中的小型龙虾状动物（小龙虾）

normalIntro.en: Prawn is stored in the mouth with a picture: a curled tail, red shell, someone peeling it at the edge of the sea.
normalIntro.cn: 记 prawn 时，把画面一并存进嘴里：卷起的尾巴、通红的壳，海边有人正剥着它。

normal.en: A king prawn is the large one that appears in tapas and curries.
normal.cn: king prawn 指出现在塔帕斯和咖喱里的那种大虾。

normal.en: A prawn cocktail is cold peeled prawns with a pink sauce, a classic starter.
normal.cn: prawn cocktail 是冷的虾仁配粉红酱汁，是经典前菜。

normal.en: Prawn farming means growing prawns in ponds for restaurants and markets.
normal.cn: prawn farming 指在池塘里养虾，供应餐馆与市场。

normal.en: To peel a prawn is to take off the shell before eating.
normal.cn: peel a prawn 就是在吃之前把壳剥掉。

normal.en: Compare shrimp, which is the everyday word in North American speech.
normal.cn: 对比 shrimp：这是北美日常口语里更常用的词。

abstract.en: Hold one big prawn and feel the thin shell crack like paper under your thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象手里握着一只大虾，薄壳在拇指下像纸一样裂开。

abstract.en: Watch a prawn snap its tail and jump backwards off the boat deck.
abstract.cn: 想象虾一弓尾巴，从船板上向后弹开。

abstract.en: Stand at a smoking grill where rows of prawns turn from grey to red.
abstract.cn: 想象站在冒烟的烤架旁，一排虾由灰转红。

examples.en: She ordered a bowl of noodles topped with grilled prawns.
examples.cn: 她点了一碗盖着烤虾的面条。

examples.en: Prawn farming has damaged stretches of coastal mangrove forest.
examples.cn: 对虾养殖已经破坏了沿海的红树林。

examples.en: He served the soup with a single prawn floating on top.
examples.cn: 他端上的汤面上浮着一只虾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「袍」——虾煮熟后披上红色外袍，宛如穿袍的小将军；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语词，词源不确定，最早记录约为十四世纪，拼作 prayne；一般认为取自古法语或北欧方言中的同类小虾肉食名，但没有可靠证据，只能确认它与「小壳可食的海洋动物」这一义域紧密相连。

sensesIntro.en: Prawn starts as the name of an animal, becomes the name of a dish, narrows in local cooking to one signature plate, and widens at last to a nickname and a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: prawn 从动物名出发，先成为菜名，再在地方菜系里收窄成一道招牌，最后又向外扩展为绰号和一个动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a prawn curled into a red crescent on a griddle.
core.cn: 核心意象：虾在铁板上蜷成一弯红色的月牙。

branches.en: The animal itself is the base sense.
branches.cn: 动物本体是最基础的义项。

branches.en: Food and regional cooking turn the creature into a plate.
branches.cn: 食物与地方烹饪把动物变成了一盘菜。

branches.en: Smallness and a curled shape let the word skip to a person.
branches.cn: 体积小、身子蜷，让这个词能跳到人身上。

branches.en: If prawns are the catch, then prawn can also be the work of catching.
branches.cn: 虾是渔获，那么捕虾也可以是这个词的动词用法。

branches.en: The animal and the catching of it belong to the same sea economy.
branches.cn: 动物与捕捞它这件事同属一条海洋经济链。

intro.en: Prawn is a plain English noun with no productive affix, but English has grown a few derived forms around it.
intro.cn: prawn 是单纯的英语名词，本身不含能产词缀，但英语已围绕它长出少数派生形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for prawn, so no Latin relatives are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: prawn 没有拉丁语来源，因此下面不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a small sea animal used as food
items.meaningCN: 可食用的小型海洋动物
items.example: Prawn is the borrowed base word.
items.exampleCN: prawn 是借入的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -s forms prawns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 prawns。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms prawnish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 构成 prawnish。

items.example: Prawnish describes a taste or a look.
items.exampleCN: prawnish 形容虾的味道或样子。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms prawny.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 prawny。

items.example: Prawny is used mostly in speech.
items.exampleCN: prawny 多见于口语。

items.meaning: a swimming stroke named for the shape of a prawn
items.meaningCN: 因形似虾而得名的泳姿
items.example: The compound prawn-crawl names a swim style.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 prawn-crawl 指一种泳姿。

items.meaning: a cold starter of peeled prawns in sauce
items.example: The compound prawn cocktail names a starter.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 prawn cocktail 指一道前菜。

definition_zh: 不稳固的；危险的；不确定的；靠不住的；勉强的
definition_en: not safe or certain, and likely to fall, fail, or change at any moment
core_image: 一个人站在晃动的梯子上，脚下只有半格踏板，手什么也没抓
scene: 脚手架在大风里轻轻摇晃，两个工人缩在高处的窄板上，谁也不敢往下看。Two workers inched along the high beams, and the footing underneath them felt precarious with every gust.
sceneCN: 这里 precarious 是「不稳固的」（第 1 个义项：物理上站不稳、随时可能失足）；句意：两名工人沿着高处横梁慢慢挪动，每一阵风都让他们脚下更觉不稳。

pos.zh: 不稳固的；摇摇欲坠的
危险的；不确定的；靠不住的

derivatives.zh: precarious 加后缀 -ly 构成的副词，义为「摇摇欲坠地；岌岌可危地」
precarious 加后缀 -ness 构成的名词，义为「不稳定性；不可靠性」
由拉丁语词干 precari 加后缀 -ity 构成的较新名词，多指工作与生活缺乏保障

senses.title: Physically unsteady
senses.definition: supported so weakly or held in such an awkward position that it may fall at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 支撑薄弱或所处位置别扭，随时可能倒下或失足的
senses.example: The ladder rested on a precarious pile of bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 梯子架在一堆摇摇晃晃的砖上。
senses.why: The core image is borrowed grip: whatever is precarious is held only by a courtesy, not by solid support.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是「借来的支撑」：东西只是勉强被托着，稍一松手就会落空，所以最直接的义项是物理上的不稳。

senses.title: Dependent on another
senses.titleCN: 靠别人给的；仰人鼻息的
senses.definition: enjoying a right or a good only through another person, without owning it or having a lasting claim
senses.definitionCN: 只靠他人给予而享有的权利或好处，自己并无所有权或长久依据
senses.example: They lived in the house on a precarious lease from a cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠表亲给的一份随时可变动的租约住着那房子。
senses.why: Medieval Latin precaria named land held at a lord or bishop discretion, so what depends on another favour is literally held by request.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语用 precaria 指靠领主或主教一句话才给的地，靠的是「祈请」而不是权利，于是「靠别人给的」便从「借来的支撑」里长出来。

senses.title: Uncertain in outcome
senses.definition: so uncertain that the result may go either way and no one can promise it
senses.definitionCN: 结果无法确定、两种走向都有可能，没人敢打包票的
senses.example: The team clings to a precarious lead with ten minutes left.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛只剩十分钟，球队勉强守着一个并不稳妥的领先。
senses.why: If the support can vanish, the future built on it can vanish too, so unsteady ground turns into an uncertain outcome.
senses.whyCN: 支撑既然随时可能消失，架在上面的未来也就不牢靠；地不稳，于是果也不定，词义就从脚下移到了结果上。

senses.title: Risky to health or life
senses.definition: involving real danger to safety, health, or life
senses.definitionCN: 确实危及安全、健康或生命的
senses.example: Many miners work in precarious conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 许多矿工在危险的条件下工作。
senses.why: An unsteady place is also a dangerous place, so the emphasis slides from instability to the harm that instability threatens.
senses.whyCN: 站不稳的地方必然也是危险的地方，词的着重点便从「不稳」滑向「不稳会带来伤害」，于是这层意思带有明显的安全含义。

senses.title: Insecure in work or money
senses.titleCN: 没有保障的；朝不保夕的
senses.definition: lacking security in a job or an income, so that losing it would be sudden and grave
senses.definitionCN: 工作或收入缺少保障，一旦失去便突然且严重
senses.example: Gig workers often face precarious income from month to month.
senses.exampleCN: 零工工作者的收入常常月月没有保障。
senses.why: Modern debate attached the word to jobs without contracts or benefits, where the ground can disappear at any moment.
senses.whyCN: 现代讨论把它固定到没有合同、没有福利的工作上：那样的生活正是「脚下的地随时可能被抽走」，不稳定的事实变成了一种社会处境的标签。

senses.title: A doubtful claim or argument
senses.titleCN: 站不住脚的；依据可疑的
senses.definition: resting on evidence or reasoning that is weak enough to be overturned
senses.definitionCN: 建立在薄弱到可能被推翻的证据或推理之上的
senses.example: The report draws a precarious conclusion from thin data.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告仅凭薄弱的数据就得出一个站不住脚的结论。
senses.why: An argument stands on evidence as a body stands on ground, so a weak case is a case with precarious footing.
senses.whyCN: 论证像人一样要站在证据上；证据越薄，站得越险，于是「论点不牢」与「脚下不稳」共用同一个隐喻。

intro.en: Precarious comes from Latin precarius, meaning obtained by entreaty, and from the verb precari, to beg.
intro.cn: precarious 来自拉丁语 precarius（靠恳求得来的），源头是动词 precari（恳求、乞求）。

items.en: Precari means to beg or to entreat, and its noun prex, with the stem prec-, names a prayer.
items.cn: precari 意为恳求、乞求，其名词 prex（词干 prec-）指祈祷或请求。

items.en: Precarius means given in answer to a request and therefore held at another will.
items.cn: precarius 意为应人之求才给予的，因而掌握在他人意志之下。

items.en: Precaria names land granted on petition, which the holder must give up when the granter asks.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 precaria 指应申请授予的土地，授予者要回时持有人必须让出。

items.en: English borrows the word as precarious and keeps the legal sense of held by favour.
items.cn: 英语以 precarious 借入该词，保留了「凭他人恩惠持有」的法律含义。

items.en: The word widens from favours to footholds, then to outcomes, health, and jobs.
items.cn: 词义从「恩惠」扩展到「落脚处」，再扩展到结果、健康与工作。

note.en: Precarious is a formal adjective that shares the prec- stem with precaution and precedent in spelling only, and stands beside risky, fragile and unstable in meaning.
note.cn: precarious 是正式形容词，在拼写上有 pre- 开头这一点与 precaution、precedent 相近但词源各异，在意义上与 risky、fragile、unstable 站在一处。

entries.definition: in a way that is likely to fall or fail
entries.definitionCN: 摇摇欲坠地；岌岌可危地

entries.definition: a step taken in advance to prevent harm
entries.definitionCN: 预防措施（只是拼写相近，词源不同：来自 prae- 与 cavere）

entries.definition: the state of having no security in work or income
entries.definitionCN: 工作与收入缺乏保障的状态

entries.definition: involving the chance of loss or harm
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的；可能出事的

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的

entries.definition: not firmly fixed and likely to change or fall
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定的；易变的

normalIntro.en: Precarious is the feeling of a foot that has found the edge but not the ground.
normalIntro.cn: precarious 就是一脚踩到了边缘、却还没踩实地面的那种感觉。

normal.en: A precarious position is one that could collapse at any second.
normal.cn: precarious position 指随时可能垮掉的处境。

normal.en: Precarious employment means work with no contract and no security.
normal.cn: precarious employment 指没有合同、没有保障的工作。

normal.en: Precarious balance describes a scale that could tip either way.
normal.cn: precarious balance 描述一种随时会倒向任一侧的平衡。

normal.en: The adverb precariously means in a way that is barely holding.
normal.cn: 副词 precariously 表示「好不容易才撑住地」。

normal.en: The Latin stem precari means to beg, so being precarious is holding something by favour, not by right.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词干 precari 意为恳求，所以 precarious 意味着靠恩惠而非权利持有某物。

abstract.en: Picture a chair balanced on two legs while someone sits on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子只用两条腿撑着，上面还坐着人。

abstract.en: Feel a hand-stop on a steep slope that will not last another second.
abstract.cn: 想象在陡坡上抓到一个支撑点，而它下一秒就会松。

abstract.en: Watch a toy tower with one block pulled almost all the way out.
abstract.cn: 想象一座积木塔，其中一块几乎被抽空。

examples.en: The cup sat precariously on the edge of the shelf.
examples.cn: 杯子摇摇欲坠地搁在架子边缘。

examples.en: After the storm, the family lived in a precarious wooden shelter.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，这家人住在一间摇摇晃晃的木棚里。

examples.en: His grasp of the language is still precarious after a few classes.
examples.cn: 上了几节课，他对这门语言的掌握仍不牢靠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不理卡瑞」——脚下的地不理卡瑞，卡瑞一松就摔，所以是不稳的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 precari（恳求、祈求）→ 形容词 precarius（应请给予的、靠他人恩准的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 precaria（凭申请获得的土地）→ 英语 precarious。核心义是「靠别人的一句允诺才得到的」，引申为「支撑可疑、随时可能落空」。

sensesIntro.en: Precarious begins as a legal word for land held by favour, turns into the physical image of an unsteady footing, and then spreads to outcomes, danger, work, and arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: precarious 最初是法律词，指靠恩准持有的土地；后转化为「落脚处不稳」这个具体画面，再扩展到结果、危险、工作与论证之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that grips a rail that is already coming loose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手抓着已经松动的栏杆。

branches.en: A footing held by nothing solid is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 没有实底可踏，是这个词的物理义项。

branches.en: A right held by favour is the oldest legal sense.
branches.cn: 靠恩惠持有的权利是最古老的法律义项。

branches.en: An unsteady base becomes an uncertain result.
branches.cn: 地基不稳，便延伸为结果不确定。

branches.en: Danger is what follows when the support gives way.
branches.cn: 支撑一旦塌陷，随之而来的就是危险。

branches.en: Jobs and arguments both stand on ground that can be pulled away.
branches.cn: 工作与论证都站在随时可被抽走的地面上。

intro.en: Precarious carries the Latin stem prec- of prayer and request, with the adjective suffix -ious marking a quality.
intro.cn: precarious 带着拉丁语表示「祈祷、请求」的词干 prec-，再由形容词后缀 -ious 标记性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin precari means to beg, its noun prex means a prayer, and precarius means obtained by entreaty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 precari 意为恳求，名词 prex 意为祈祷，形容词 precarius 意为靠恳求得来的。

items.example: Precari gives the whole family its begging image.
items.exampleCN: precari 提供整个词族的「恳求」意象。

items.example: Prex has the stem prec-, which passes into English.
items.exampleCN: prex 的词干 prec- 传入英语。

items.meaning: obtained by entreaty, held at another will
items.meaningCN: 靠恳求得来的；由他人意志支配的
items.example: Precarius is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: precarius 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Precaria shows the legal heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: precaria 展示了这个词的法律内核。

items.example: The pre- in precaution is a different element.
items.exampleCN: precaution 中的 pre- 是另一来源，与 prec- 无关。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms adjectives such as precarious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 构成 precarious 这类形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb precariously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 precariously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms precariousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 precariousness。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms precarity in recent usage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成较新的 precarity。

definition_en: an earlier action, decision, or case that later people can point to as a model or a rule
core_image: 法官翻开一叠旧案卷，手指停在一页判决上：前面的判过了，后面的照着来
scene: 法庭上，双方律师反复翻看同一份旧判决书，法官摘下眼镜，让大家安静下来听她读那一页。The judge read out the ruling and reminded both sides that the precedent still bound the court.
sceneCN: 这里 precedent 是「先例、判例」（第 1 个义项：法院此前的判决，后来的法官必须据此裁断）；句意：法官宣读了那份判决，并提醒双方这个判例仍然约束本法庭。

pos.zh: 先例；判例；范例；惯例

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 un- 与 precedent 的形容词式 precedented 构成，义为「史无前例的」
由 precedent 加后缀 -ial 构成，法律义为「有判例效力的」
由 precedent 加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「有先例的」

senses.title: An earlier court ruling
senses.definition: a past decision of a court that later judges are expected to follow in similar cases
senses.definitionCN: 法院过去的判决，后来审理类似案件的法官应当遵循
senses.example: The ruling set a precedent that all employers must note.
senses.exampleCN: 这项判决确立了一个所有雇主都必须注意的判例。
senses.why: The word goes before the law, so the earlier case that should guide a later one gets the name directly.
senses.whyCN: pre- 表示「在前」，法庭上走在最前面、该被后案照着办的那份判决，自然就被叫做先例。

senses.title: A model to be copied
senses.definition: a person or action that later people follow as a model of how to do something
senses.definitionCN: 后来者模仿其做法、当作榜样的某个人或某种做法
senses.example: Her smooth transfer of power became a precedent for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 她平稳的权力交接成了这个地区的范例。
senses.why: If a court can go first, anyone can: the model sense spreads the word from law to any field where an earlier act guides a later one.
senses.whyCN: 法院能走在前面，别的领域也能：只要先做的事被后来者照着办，「先例」就从法律扩散成普通的范例。

senses.title: The precedent-setting action
senses.titleCN: 开创先例之举；首开例先的事
senses.definition: the first action that makes something acceptable or expected from then on
senses.definitionCN: 第一次做出、从此让某事被接受或被期待的行为
senses.example: Giving one student extra time set a precedent for the whole course.
senses.exampleCN: 给一个学生延长时间，就为整门课开了个先例。
senses.why: Precedent can name not only the old model but the fresh first step that creates a rule for the future, hence the phrase set a precedent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指旧的参照，也指那个「第一次」本身：正因为这个举动会被后人效法，它才成了先例，所以英语说「set a precedent」。

senses.title: A customary practice
senses.definition: a long-established way of doing something that people now expect to be kept
senses.definitionCN: 由来已久、人们如今期待被沿用下去的做法
senses.example: By long precedent, the chair speaks last at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 按长期惯例，主席在会议最后发言。
senses.why: Once a first act has been followed many times, the single case thickens into a habit, and precedent comes to mean custom.
senses.whyCN: 第一件事被一遍遍照着做之后，个案便沉淀为习惯，于是先例在中国语境里也常常等同于「惯例」。

senses.title: A rule taken as settled
senses.definition: a decision or view treated as settled because it has been accepted again and again
senses.definitionCN: 因一再被接受而被视为已经定下来的决定或看法
senses.example: It is now a precedent in the company that remote work is allowed.
senses.exampleCN: 如今在这家公司，允许远程工作已成定规。
senses.why: The force of precedent is expectation, and expectation hardened over time becomes something people rely on as a rule.
senses.whyCN: 先例的力量来自「大家都期待如此」；期待反复被确认，就硬化为可以引用的定规，词的抽象程度因此又上一层。

intro.en: Precedent comes from Latin praecedere, to go before, made from prae- (before) and cedere (to go).
intro.cn: precedent 来自拉丁语 praecedere（走在前面），由 prae-（在前）与 cedere（走）构成。

items.en: Praecurrere shows the same prae- and a running verb, meaning to run ahead.
items.cn: praecurrere 用同样的 prae- 加「跑」的动词，意为跑在前面。

items.en: Praecedere means to go before another in place or time, and praecedens names what is in front.
items.cn: praecedere 意为在位置或时间上走在前头，praecedens 则指前面那件事。

items.en: The adjective praecedent-, going before, passes through French as precedent.
items.cn: 形容词词干 praecedent- 表示「在前的」，经法语以 precedent 进入英语。

items.en: English uses precedent first as an adjective and then as a noun in the law courts.
items.cn: 英语先把它作形容词用，随后在法庭上把它用作名词。

items.en: The law of precedent spreads to business, politics, and sport as a general habit word.
items.cn: 判例法中的先例观念扩散到商业、政治与体育，成为一个通用的「惯例」词。

note.en: Precedent is a noun from the family of precede and precede forms such as precedence, and it stands beside example, custom and landmark in meaning.
note.cn: precedent 是 precede 词族里的一员，与 precedence 等同族词拼写相近，在意义上与 example、custom、landmark 站在一处。

entries.definition: to come or go before someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 先于；走在……之前（precedent 的动词同源词）

entries.definition: the right to be treated as more important than others
entries.definitionCN: 优先权；优先地位（与 precedent 拼写相近、同源，但读音与义项不同）

entries.definition: never having happened before
entries.definitionCN: 史无前例的（由 un- 加 precedented 构成）

entries.definition: a person or thing that shows how others should act
entries.definitionCN: 榜样；值得效法的例子

entries.definition: a long-established way of behaving in a group
entries.definitionCN: 习俗；惯例

entries.definition: an event or decision that marks a turning point
entries.definitionCN: 里程碑式的事件或判决

normalIntro.en: Precedent is the footstep in front of you: it shows the way, and walking in it becomes the rule.
normalIntro.cn: precedent 就是走在前面留下的一串脚印：它指了路，照着走就成了规矩。

normal.en: To set a precedent is to be the first, and to make others follow.
normal.cn: set a precedent 就是开个头，让后来者照着办。

normal.en: A legal precedent binds later courts in similar cases.
normal.cn: legal precedent 在类似案件中约束后来的法院。

normal.en: Without precedent means there has never been such a thing before.
normal.cn: without precedent 表示从来没有过这样的事。

normal.en: The adjective unprecedented is built on the same noun and means the opposite of having a precedent.
normal.cn: 形容词 unprecedented 由同一个名词构成，意思正好是「没有先例」。

normal.en: The Latin source praecedere means to go before, so the word is about walking ahead and leaving a track.
normal.cn: 拉丁语来源 praecedere 意为走在前头，所以这个词讲的正是先走一步、留下足迹。

abstract.en: Picture a long line of footprints with your own pair falling in step behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象一串长长的脚印，你的一双正落在它们后面。

abstract.en: See a heavy stamp press a wax seal into paper, and the next sheet shows the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚重印章在纸上压下印痕，下一张纸也印出同样的记号。

abstract.en: Imagine a list on the wall where each new name is written under the one above it.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一张名单，新名字总写在上面那个的下面。

examples.en: Her speech set a precedent for how future leaders should behave.
examples.cn: 她的演讲为将来的领导人该如何行事开创了先例。

examples.en: Judges in this country must follow the precedent of higher courts.
examples.cn: 这个国家的法官必须遵循上级法院的判例。

examples.en: There is no precedent for such a merger in local banking.
examples.cn: 当地银行业此前没有这样的合并先例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞西登」——普瑞西先登上台阶，后到的人便照他的落点踩着上；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ cedere（走）→ 动词 praecedere（走在前面）→ 形容词词干 praecedent-（在前的）→ 法语 precedent → 英语 precedent。核心义是「走在前头、可供后来者照着走的那一步」。

sensesIntro.en: Precedent starts as an earlier court ruling, widens to any model worth copying, names the first step that creates the rule, and finally settles into custom and settled practice.
sensesIntro.cn: precedent 从法院此前的判决出发，扩展到任何值得效法的范例，又指那次开创规矩的第一步，最后沉淀为惯例与定规。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of footprints, the first one the deepest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串脚印，第一枚踩得最深。

branches.en: A court decision that goes before is the technical core.
branches.cn: 法院走在前面作出的判决，是这个词的技术核心义。

branches.en: Any model worth copying takes the name outside the law.
branches.cn: 任何值得照办的范例都会让这个词走出法律领域。

branches.en: The first act that creates the pattern is named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 那一次开创新格局的举动，也用同一个名词来称呼。

branches.en: Repeated following turns a single case into custom.
branches.cn: 反复照办之后，单个案件沉淀成了惯例。

branches.en: A model and a settled rule differ only in how firmly people rely on them.
branches.cn: 范例与定规只差在人们依靠它的程度。

intro.en: Precedent breaks into the Latin prefix prae-, the Latin root ced- meaning go, and the suffix -ent forming an adjective or noun.
intro.cn: precedent 可拆成拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）、词根 ced-（走）与后缀 -ent（构成形容词或名词）。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- means before, cedere means to go or yield, and praecedere means to go before.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 意为在前，cedere 意为走、让，praecedere 意为走在前面。

items.example: The prefix prae- marks what comes first.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 标出先在者。

items.meaning: to go, to move, to yield
items.example: Cedere supplies the walking image.
items.exampleCN: cedere 提供「走」的画面。

items.example: Praecedere is the direct source verb.
items.exampleCN: praecedere 是直接来源动词。

items.example: The stem praecedent- passes into French and English.
items.exampleCN: 词干 praecedent- 传入法语与英语。

items.meaningCN: 做……的（构成形容词或名词）
items.example: The suffix -ent turns the verb into a noun of result.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 把动词变为结果名词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms precedented.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 precedented。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unprecedented.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unprecedented。

items.meaning: the state of being earlier or more important
items.example: Precedence is the sibling noun from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: precedence 是出自同一动词的姊妹名词。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms precedential.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 precedential。
